ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r8.claim: Reports describe Medina Jewish scholars who privately affirmed Muhammad as true and urged others to follow him, but feared losing gifts and taxes; some urged charity, obedience, prayer, and zakat without practicing those duties themselves. The author says one or all such cases occasioned the verse.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r8.anchor: asr-ı sa‘âdette Medine’deki ahbâr-ı Yehûd’dan bazıları kendilerine gizlice gelip “Muhammed hakkında ne dersin?” diye istifsar edenlere “doğrudur, haktır” derler

ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r9.claim: The verse asks how people can command abundant goodness while forgetting themselves even as they continually read the Torah; the author also renders the question as asking whether they will learn sense.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r9.anchor: Acayip, siz nâsa birr yani bol bol iyilik emreder de kendinizi unutur musunuz?

ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r10.claim: The first reason is practical contradiction: the purpose of enjoining good is to guide others, but neglecting oneself deprives oneself of guidance and risks damnation.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r10.anchor: başkasını irşad edip de kendisini unutmak ve kendisini iyilikten, irşaddan mahrum etmek

ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r11.claim: The second reason is that a teacher who will not heed his own advice refutes himself and his learning, while misleading people he claims to guide; this is another contradiction and a kind of deception.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r11.anchor: kendisi kendi emrini, kendi nasihatini dinlememek, kendini ve ilmini fiilen tekzibdir.

ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r12.claim: The third reason is that acting against one's advice destroys its value and alienates listeners, like cutting the branch one sits on.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r12.anchor: verdiği emr ü nasihatin kendisi hilâfını yapmak onun kıymetini kırmak ve herkesi ondan tenfir eylemektir.

ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r13.claim: Enjoining good remains good and obligatory; the verse censures forgetting oneself, but does not forbid a sinner from sincerely advising others when he speaks truthfully. It sharply warns preachers to take themselves seriously first.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r13.anchor: bu âyet fâsığın doğru söylemek, sözünde cidden iyiyi söylemek şartıyla vaaz etmesini, emr bi’l-ma‘rûf yapmasını men‘etmemekle beraber

ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r14.speaker: Buhârî ve Müslim
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r14.claim: They report a man brought on Judgment Day and cast into the Fire, where he circles like a millstone; when asked why he preached good and forbade evil without practicing it, he admits his hypocrisy.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r14.anchor: Buhârî ve Müslim’de bu babda şu hadîs-i şerîf rivayet olunmuştur

ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r15.claim: Birr means broad goodness: as a noun it is abundant good and as a verbal noun expansion in goodness, derived from a word for spaciousness; it encompasses every good.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r15.anchor: geniş iyilik, bol bol iyilik etmek demek olan “birr” her türlü iyiliğe, her nevi hayra şâmildir

ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r16.claim: The author classifies birr into three kinds: worship of God, care for relatives, and good dealings with friends.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r16.anchor: birr üçtür: Allah’a ibadette birr, akrabaya riayette birr, ahbâbına muâmelede birr.

ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r17.claim: This exhortation ratifies Islam's high moral and intellectual seriousness, especially for scholars, rulers, and judges; its placement after prayer, zakat, and congregation points to their effect on moral refinement and criticizes scholars who do not practice their learning.
ELMALILI:2:40-46#2/r17.anchor: bilhassa ilmiyle âmil olmamak Benî İsrâil ahbârının şi‘ârı olduğunu anlatmıştır

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p24/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p24/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p24/r1.claim: Jews of Medina urged Muslim in-laws, relatives, and milk kin to keep their faith and follow Muhammad, while they themselves did not act on that advice.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p24/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية الكلبي عن أبي صالح بالإسناد الذي ذكر: نزلت في يهود أهل المدينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r1.claim: Amr can mean a command or an affair; the imperative drops its initial hamza without a conjunction, while retaining it after waw or fa is better.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r1.anchor: الأمر: طلب إيجاد الفعل، ويطلق على الشأن، والفعل منه: أمر يأمر، على: فعل يفعل، وتحذف فاؤه في الأمر منه بغير لام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r2.claim: Amara takes two objects, one directly and one through a preposition; certain verbs allow omission of that preposition before the second object, but the pattern is limited and not productive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r2.anchor: وهو مما يتعدى إلى مفعولين: أحدهما بنفسه، والآخر بحرف جر. ويجوز حذف ذلك الحرف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r3.claim: Birr can mean kinship, obedience, the heart, a fox's young, or a cat; a rajaz line uses the verb for treating people well.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r3.anchor: البر: الصلة، وأيضا: الطاعة. قال الراجز: لا هم رب إن بكرا دونكا ... يبرك الناس ويفخرونكا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r4.claim: Birr toward one's father means honoring him; forms of the root also describe a fulfilled oath or pilgrimage and gathering kinds of good.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r4.anchor: وبر والده: أجله وأعظمه. يبره: على وزن فعل يفعل، ورجل بار، وبر، وبرت يمينه، وبر حجه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r5.claim: Birr denotes expansiveness in kindness and goodness, covers every good, and is related to words for spaciousness; ibrār can mean prevailing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r5.anchor: والبر سعة المعروف والخير، ومنه: البر والبرية للسعة. ويتناول كل خير، والإبرار: الغلبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r6.claim: An unnamed poet uses yabrūn to attest the sense of prevailing over someone who resists.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r6.anchor: قال الشاعر: ويبرون على الآبي المبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r7.claim: Nisyān is opposite remembrance and can mean a lapse after knowledge or simply leaving something; its verb normally takes one object but can be suspended like ʿalima.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r7.anchor: النسيان: ضد الذكر، وهو السهو الحادث بعد حصول العلم، ويطلق أيضا على الترك، وضده الفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r8.claim: An unnamed poet illustrates nisyān used with an attached question in the manner of ʿalima; the author says the verse is ambiguous.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r8.anchor: وقد يعلق نسي حملا على علم، قال الشاعر: ومن أنتم إنا نسينا من انتم ... وريحكم من أي ريح الأعاصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r9.claim: Tilawa means recitation because verses, words, or letters follow one another in recitation; the root also means following, as a calf follows its mother.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r9.anchor: التلاوة: القراءة، وسميت بها لأن الآيات أو الكلمات أو الحروف يتلو بعضها بعضا في الذكر. والتلو: التبع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r10.claim: ʿAql is perception that prevents error, like a camel's hobble or a refuge; ʿaql also means blood money, possibly because camels are tied or the payment restrains retaliation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r10.anchor: العقل: الإدراك المانع من الخطأ، ومنه عقال البعير، يمنعه من التصرف، والمعقل: مكان يمتنع فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r11.claim: ʿAql can also name a decorated garment; a poet's line describes its patterned fabric.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p293#2/r11.anchor: والعقل: ثوب موشى، قال الشاعر: عقلا ورقما تظل الطير تتبعه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r1.claim: ʿIqāl means the year's zakat or levy, as illustrated by a poet's line about collecting one year's amount and then two.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r1.anchor: والعقال: زكاة العام، قال الشاعر: سعى عقالا فلم يترك لنا سبدا ... فكيف لو قد سعى عمرو عقالين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r2.claim: ʿAqnqal sand is compacted and does not collapse.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r12.claim: The interrogative hamza is formally a question but here conveys rebuke and censure for commanding good while neglecting oneself; the same applies to forbidding wrong while doing it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r12.anchor: الهمزة: للاستفهام وضعا، وشابها هنا التوبيخ والتقريع لأن المعنى: الإنكار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r13.claim: Abu al-Aswad's verse condemns forbidding a trait while practicing it; another poet advises beginning by correcting oneself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r13.anchor: قول أبي الأسود: لا تنه عن خلق وتأتي مثله ... عار عليك إذا فعلت عظيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r14.claim: Birr is interpreted as holding to the Messenger's religion while not following him, or following the Torah while denying its description of him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r14.anchor: الثبات على دين رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهم لا يتبعونه، أو اتباع التوراة وهم يخالفونها في جحدهم صفته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r15.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r15.claim: Qatada, Ibn Jurayj, and al-Suddi include exhorting people to give charity while being miserly among the meanings of birr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r15.anchor: وروي عن قتادة وابن جريج والسدي: أو على الصدقة ويبخلون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r16.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r16.claim: Qatada, Ibn Jurayj, and al-Suddi also include exhorting truthfulness while not speaking truthfully.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r16.anchor: وروي عن قتادة وابن جريج والسدي: أو على الصدقة ويبخلون، أو على الصدق وهم لا يصدقون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r17.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r17.claim: Qatada, Ibn Jurayj, and al-Suddi also explain it as urging companions to pray and give zakat without doing so themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r17.anchor: أو حض أصحابهم على الصلاة والزكاة ولا يأتونهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r18.speaker: السلمي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r18.claim: Al-Sulami reads the rebuke as demanding inward realities while one's heart lacks even their outward forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r18.anchor: وقال السلمي: أتطالبون الناس بحقائق المعاني وأنتم قلوبكم خالية عن ظواهر رسومها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r19.speaker: القشيري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r19.claim: Al-Qushayri paraphrases the rebuke as urging others to hurry while accepting delay oneself, or calling people toward God while remaining behind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r19.anchor: وقال القشيري: أتحرضون الناس على البدار وترضون بالتخلف؟ وقال: أتدعون الخلق إلينا وتقعدون عنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r20.claim: The present tense suggests that their hypocritical habit was continuous or frequent even though the conduct had already occurred.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p294/r20.anchor: وأتى بالمضارع في: أتأمرون، وإن كان قد وقع ذلك منهم لأنه يفهم منه في الاستعمال في كثير من المواضع: الديمومة وكثرة التلبس بالفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r1.claim: Calling their neglect 'forgetting' intensifies the charge by portraying the duty as absent from their minds; 'themselves' likewise reinforces their extreme heedlessness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r1.anchor: الترك، فكأنه لا يجري لهم على بال، وعلق النساء بالأنفس توكيدا للمبالغة في الغفلة المفرطة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r2.claim: Al-anfus may mean their own persons or their people and community.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r2.anchor: والأنفس هنا: ذواتهم، وقيل: جماعتهم وأهل ملتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r3.claim: Reading scripture means direct engagement with it and knowledge of its contents, making their guidance of others alongside their own disobedience especially blameworthy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r3.anchor: أي أنكم مباشرو الكتاب وقارئوه، وعالمون بما انطوى عليه، فكيف امتثلتموه بالنسبة إلى غيركم؟ وخالفتموه أنفسكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r4.claim: The majority identify the Book as the Torah and Gospel, both of which prohibit this shameful trait.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r4.anchor: والكتاب هنا: التوراة والإنجيل، وفيهما النهي عن هذا الوصف الذميم، وهذا قول الجمهور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r5.claim: A minority identifies the Book as the Qur'an and takes the passage as a shift from addressing the People of the Book to believers; the author finds this unlikely because the whole passage appears directed to the People of the Book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r5.anchor: وقيل: الكتاب هنا القرآن، قالوا: ويكون قد انصرف من خطاب أهل الكتاب إلى خطاب المؤمنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r6.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r6.claim: Sibawayh and the grammarians say the conjunction originally preceded the interrogative hamza, which takes initial position and is therefore advanced.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r6.anchor: مذهب سيبويه والنحويين: أن أصل الكلام كان تقديم حرف العطف على الهمزة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the conjunction stays in its normal position and an unspoken clause is understood between it and the hamza, avoiding inversion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r7.anchor: وزعم الزمخشري أن الواو والفاء وثم بعد الهمزة واقعة موقعها، ولا تقديم ولا تأخير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari later returned in some works to the grammarians' analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p296/r8.anchor: وقد رجع عن هذا القول في بعض تصانيفه إلى قول الجماعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r1.claim: A rational person secures personal salvation before trying to secure others'; advising others while withholding benefit from oneself contradicts sound judgment, especially when eternal salvation is at stake.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r1.anchor: فإذا صدر من الإنسان تحصيل المصلحة لغيره، ومنع ذلك لنفسه، كان ذلك خارجا عن أفعال العقلاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r2.claim: A poet illustrates that someone who cannot restrain his own tongue cannot be a guardian of anything else.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r2.anchor: ألا ترى إلى قول الشاعر: إذا المرء لم يخزن عليه لسانه ... فليس على شيء سواه بخزان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r3.claim: One explanation of 'will you not reason?' asks whether they can stop themselves from falling into this ruinous state.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r3.anchor: أفلا تعقلون: أفلا تمنعون أنفسكم من مواقعة هذه الحال المردية بكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r4.claim: Another explanation asks whether they understand the ugliness of disobeying God by refusing to follow and believe Muhammad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r4.anchor: أو أفلا تفهمون قبح ما تأتون من معصية ربكم في اتباع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والإيمان به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r5.claim: Other explanations gloss the phrase as desisting from wrongdoing, since reason forbids ugly acts, or returning to what is better.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r5.anchor: أو أفلا تنتهون، لأن العقل ينهى عن القبيح، أو أفلا ترجعون، لأن العقل يراد إلى الأحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r6.claim: Other explanations ask whether they recognize the truth and follow it, or realize that the punishment will return upon them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r6.anchor: أو أفلا تعقلون أنه حق فتتبعونه، أو أن وبال ذلك عليكم راجع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r7.claim: Further explanations ask whether they refrain from sin, recognize the irrationality of commanding good without doing it, or notice how ugly their conduct is.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r7.anchor: أو أفلا تمتنعون من المعاصي، أو أفلا تعقلون، إذ ليس في قضية العقل أن تأمر بالمعروف ولا تأتيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r8.claim: Their conduct appears as if they had lost reason, since sound minds reject and repel it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r8.anchor: وكأنكم في ذلك مسلوبو العقل، لأن العقول تأباه وتدفعه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r9.claim: Enjoining right and forbidding wrong aim to guide people toward benefit and warn them from harm; preaching without self-reform is contradictory and can make listeners distrust the sermon and drift toward sin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r9.anchor: والمقصود من الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر: الإرشاد إلى المنفعة والتحذير عن المفسدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r10.claim: A poem says an admonition will not be accepted until the preacher first takes it to heart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r10.anchor: وأنشدوا: مواعظ الواعظ لن تقبلا ... حتى يعيها قبله أولا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r11.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r11.claim: Ali says two people broke his back: a shameless scholar and a devout but ignorant person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r11.anchor: وقال علي كرم الله وجهه: قصم ظهري رجلان: عالم متهتك، وجاهل متنسك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r12.claim: The verse and the parallel 'why do you say what you do not do?' do not prove that a sinner may not enjoin right and forbid wrong.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r12.anchor: ولا دليل في الآية لمن استدل بها على أنه ليس للعاصي أن يأمر بالمعروف وينهى عن المنكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r13.speaker: المعتزلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r13.claim: The Muʿtazilites cite the rebuke to argue that human acts are not created by God, since they think rebuke only fits acts performed by the people themselves; the author calls the theological question difficult and leaves it to kalam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r13.anchor: ولا للمعتزلة في أن فعل العبد غير مخلوق لله تعالى، قالوا: التوبيخ لا يحسن إلا إذا كانوا فاعلي أفعالهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r14.claim: Although addressed to the Israelites, the warning applies generally in meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r14.anchor: وهذا الإنكار والتوبيخ والتقريع، وإن كان خطابا لبني إسرائيل، فهو عام من حيث المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r15.speaker: محمد بن واسع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r15.claim: Muhammad ibn Wasi reports that people in Paradise looked upon people in Hell and began confronting them about the instructions that had led the latter to Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p297/r15.anchor: وعن محمد بن واسع: بلغني أن ناسا من أهل الجنة اطلعوا على

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r1.speaker: محمد بن واسع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Wasi's report concludes that the saved people followed the advice they had been given, while the people in Hell had advised others but acted differently themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p298/r1.anchor: قد كنتم تأمروننا بأشياء عملناها فدخلنا الجنة، قالوا: كنا نأمركم بها ونخالف إلى غيرها

QASHANI:2:44-46/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:44-46/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:44-46/r1.claim: Righteousness is beautiful action that purifies the heart and increases the soul through illumination; teachers who neglect it fail to rise from witnessing acts to witnessing attributes.
QASHANI:2:44-46/r1.anchor: الفعل الجميل الموجب لصفاء القلب، وزكاء النفس الزائد منها بالتنور

QASHANI:2:44-46/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:44-46/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:44-46/r2.claim: The book they recite is the book of their innate nature, which commands following Muhammad’s religion on the path of divine unity.
QASHANI:2:44-46/r2.anchor: كتاب فطرتكم الذي يأمركم باتباع محمد في دينه السالك بكم سبيل التوحيد

QASHANI:2:44-46/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:44-46/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:44-46/r3.claim: The question “Do you not reason?” is a severe rebuke and an incitement to their zeal.
QASHANI:2:44-46/r3.anchor: أفلا تعقلون } تعيير بالغ، وتهييج لحميتهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r1.claim: The verse was revealed about Jewish scholars who told Muslim relatives and allies to remain in their religion because Muhammad's cause was true and his speech truthful.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r1.anchor: {أتأمرون الناس بالبر} أي بالطاعة، نزلت في علماء اليهود، وذلك أن الرجل منهم كان يقول

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r2.claim: Another view addresses Jewish rabbis who told followers to hold to the Torah while themselves changing it and concealing Muhammad's description.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو خطاب لأخبارهم حيث أمروا أتباعهم بالتمسك بالتوراة، ثم خالفوا وغيروا نعت محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r3.claim: Forgetting themselves means failing to follow Muhammad, although they read the Torah containing his description.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r3.anchor: {وتنسون أنفسكم} أي تتركون أنفسكم فلا تتبعونه {وأنتم تتلون الكتاب} تقرءون التوراة فيها نعته وصفته {أفلا تعقلون}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r4.claim: The question “Will you not reason?” asks why they do not recognize the truth and follow Muhammad.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r4.anchor: التوراة فيها نعته وصفته {أفلا تعقلون} أنه حق فتتبعونه؟.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r5.claim: Reason is named from the tether that restrains a camel; reason likewise restrains its possessor from disbelief and denial.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r5.anchor: والعقل مأخوذ من عقال الدابة، وهو ما يشد به ركبة البعير فيمنعه من الشرود،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r6.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r6.claim: Anas reports that on the Night Journey the Prophet saw people whose lips were cut with fire shears; Gabriel identified them as speakers from the Prophet's community who urged good while neglecting themselves as they read scripture.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r6.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "رأيت ليلة أسري بي رجالا تقرض شفاههم بمقاريض من نار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r7.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r7.claim: Usama reports that a man in Hell will have his intestines spill out and circle like a donkey at a mill; when asked why, he admits he urged good without doing it and forbade evil while doing it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r7.anchor: قال أسامة رضي الله عنه: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "يجاء بالرجل يوم القيامة فيلقى في النار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r8.speaker: شعبة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r8.claim: Shuʿba's version of al-Aʿmash's report says the man is ground in Hell like a donkey grinding at its mill.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p88/r8.anchor: وقال شعبة عن الأعمش "فيطحن فيها كما يطحن الحمار برحاه" (3)

BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r2.claim: After recalling Israel's favors and prohibiting ingratitude and broken covenants, God rebukes their scholars for urging virtues and prohibiting vices while failing to practice what they preach.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r2.anchor: وكانوا يأمرون غيرهم بما يزعمون أنه تزكية وينهونه عما يدعون أنه تردية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r3.claim: Al-Harali defines commanding as imposing a judgment and righteousness as expansion in good deeds; forgetting is a lapse after knowledge has been gained.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r3.anchor: من الأمر وهو الإلزام بالحكم - قاله الحرالي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r4.claim: The likely target is Torah's command to follow Muhammad: scholars imposed Torah's other rulings on ordinary people while neglecting the foundational righteousness on which the rest depends.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد به حكم التوراة , كانوا يحملون عوامهم عليه وهم يعلمون دون العوام أن من حكم التوراة اتباع محمد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r5.claim: Some advised seekers to follow Muhammad but did not follow their own advice; this exposes irrationality and links their conduct to their earlier breach of covenant, confusion, and concealment.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r5.anchor: فيهم من أشار على من استهداه بالهداية لاتباع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يهدوا أنفسهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r6.claim: The clause about reciting scripture shows that the Torah's instruction to follow Muhammad is explicit, not hidden by implication, and makes a scholar's disobedience more heinous.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r6.anchor: قال الحرالي : فيه إشعار بأن أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في منطوق تلاوته ليس في خفي إفهامه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r7.claim: Tilāwa means following a speaker's utterance from its beginning; the circumstantial clause emphasizes their knowledge of scripture while they disobey.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r7.anchor: من التلاوة , وهو تتبع قول قائل أول من جهة أوليته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r8.claim: Reason grasps the realities whose outward surface the senses perceive; it is called reason because it restrains a person from stumbling into ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r8.anchor: والعقل إدراك حقائق ما نال الحس ظاهره

BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r9.claim: Their attachment to leadership made them resist becoming followers of Arabs after seeing themselves as masters of the earth, so patience is prescribed to compel them to accept following truth.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p124/r9.anchor: ما تعودت به أنفسهم من الرياسة والتقدم فلما في ذلك عليهم من المشقة أن يصيروا أتباعا للعرب

DURR-FULL:v1p158/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas tells a would-be preacher to first master three warnings against ordering righteousness while neglecting oneself, saying what one does not do, and opposing one's own counsel; he concludes that the man should begin with himself.
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه جاءه رجل فقال: يا ابن عباس إني اريد أن آمر بالمعروف وأنهى عن المنكر

DURR-FULL:v1p158/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r2.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r2.claim: Every preacher will have his sermon presented to God, who will examine the intention behind it.
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r2.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: ما خطب خطيب في الدنيا إلا سيعرض الله عليه خطبته ما أراد بها

DURR-FULL:v1p158/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r3.claim: Abu al-Darda says woe once to the person who lacks knowledge, and seven times to one who knows but does not act.
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r3.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: ويل للذي لا يعلم مرة ولو شاء الله لعلمه وويل للذي يعلم ولا يعمل سبع مرات

DURR-FULL:v1p158/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r4.claim: Ibn Masud gives the same warning: woe to the ignorant and sevenfold woe to one who knows but fails to act.
DURR-FULL:v1p158/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: ويل للذي لا يعلم ولو شاء الله لعلمه وويل لمن يعلم ثم لايعمل سبع مرات

IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r2.claim: The rebuke concerns people who forbid others to disbelieve in the prophethood and covenant they possess in the Torah while neglecting themselves.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r2.anchor: اي تنهون الناس عن الكفر بما عندكم من النبوة والعهد من التوراة .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r3.claim: The Israelites commanded obedience, piety, and righteousness while acting otherwise, so God reproached them.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : اتامرون الناس بالبر وتنسون انفسكم قال : كان بنو اسرائيل يامرون الناس بطاعة الله وبتقواه وبالبر ، ويخالفون ، فعيرهم الله .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says they commanded people to obey God while disobeying Him themselves.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r4.anchor: عن السدى : اتامرون الناس بالبر وتنسون انفسكم وأنتم تتلون الكتاب قال كانوا يامرون الناس بطاعته ، وهم يعصونه .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r5.claim: “You forget yourselves” means that you leave yourselves behind.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p101/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس : وتنسون انفسكم اي تتركون انفسكم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r1.claim: Verse 2:44 is a parenthetical rebuke between the prayer-and-alms commands and the call to seek help: their prayer among worshippers does not suffice when they fail to practice the righteousness they teach.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r1.anchor: اعتراض بين قوله : { وأقيموا الصلاة } ( البقرة : 43 ) وقوله : { واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة } ( البقرة : 45 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r2.claim: The parenthesis lacks a coordinating waw to show that its central purpose is exposing their loss and corrupt state, not simply urging them to preach righteousness consistently.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r2.anchor: وللتنبيه على كونه اعتراضا لم يقرن بالواو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r3.claim: They teach and preach as artisans or merchants perform a trade, fulfilling religious duties for the ranks and salaries they expect, without examining their own conduct.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r3.anchor: كما يقوم الصانع بصناعته والتاجر بتجارته لا يقصدون إلا إيفاء وظائفهم الدينية حقها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r4.claim: The direct address grammatically covers all Israelites, implying each proclaims religious commands but does not obey them; alternatively, collective address can assign the rebuke to only the relevant subgroup, especially their scholars.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r4.anchor: والمخاطب بقوله : { أتأمرون } جميع بني إسرائيل الذين خوطبوا من قبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r5.claim: Under the all-Israelite reading, ‘people’ may mean Arab polytheists, who listened when Jews recounted their religion; the Qur'an notes their former expectation of victory over unbelievers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r5.anchor: فإن اليهود كانوا يذكرون لهم ما جاء به دينهم والعرب كانوا يحفلون بسماع أقوالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r6.claim: Alternatively, under the all-Israelite reading, ‘people’ means everyone besides the preacher, as in the idiom ‘do as people do’ and the Qur'anic example about people gathering against you.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r6.anchor: وإما أن يكون المراد من ( الناس ) من عدا الآمر كما تقول أفعل كما يفعل الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r7.claim: If the address targets Israel's scholars, ‘people’ means ordinary Jewish followers whom the scholars command to righteousness while neglecting themselves.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r7.anchor: وعلى الوجه الثاني يكون المراد بالناس العامة من أمة اليهود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r8.claim: The scholars may also be tacitly accused of recognizing Islam's Messenger as truthful: they admonish followers but do not seek their own salvation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p474/r8.anchor: أو تعريض بأنهم يعلمون أن ما جاء به رسول الإسلام هو الحق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136/r12.claim: “Do you command people” is a rhetorical question meant as rebuke; birr gathers forms of good and obedience, each of which can itself be called birr.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136/r12.anchor: خرج مخرج الاستفهام، ومعناه التوبيخ، و «البر» يجمع وجوه الخير والطاعات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136/r13.claim: Tansawna means “you leave” or “neglect,” as in the parallel wording in al-Tawba.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136/r13.anchor: وتنسون بمعنى تتركون كما قال الله تعالى: نسوا الله فنسيهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Jewish scholars urged their followers to follow the Torah while they themselves violated it by denying its description of Muḥammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136/r14.anchor: كان الأحبار يأمرون أتباعهم ومقلديهم باتباع التوراة، وكانوا هم يخالفونها في جحدهم منها صفة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r1.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r1.claim: Some scholars directed Arab questioners toward following Muhammad while failing to follow him themselves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r1.anchor: كان الأحبار إذا استرشدهم أحد من العرب في اتباع محمد دلوه على ذلك، وهم لا يفعلونه.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says scholars urged people to obey God while committing sins themselves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: «كان الأحبار يحضون الناس على طاعة الله، وكانوا هم يواقعون المعاصي» .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r3.claim: Another group says the scholars urged charity while being miserly themselves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r3.anchor: وقالت فرقة: كانوا يحضون على الصدقة ويبخلون.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r4.claim: The phrase تتلون means that they study and read the Book.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وأنتم تتلون معناه: تدرسون وتقرءون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, تتلون can mean following the Book by emulating it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المعنى تتبعون أي في الاقتداء به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r6.claim: The Torah forbids them from the reprehensible conduct described in the verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r6.anchor: والكتاب التوراة وهي تنهاهم عما هم عليه من هذه الصفة الذميمة.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r7.claim: أفلا تعقلون asks whether they will restrain themselves from this ruinous condition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r7.anchor: أفلا تمنعون أنفسكم من مواقعة هذه الحال المردية لكم؟

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r8.claim: Reason is perception that prevents error; the word is related to a camel hobble and a place of protection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p136#2/r8.anchor: والعقل: الإدراك المانع من الخطأ مأخوذ منه عقال البعير

NAHHAS:v1p220/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p220/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p220/r2.claim: تنسون is present tense coordinated with the preceding verb; أفلا تعقلون has the same parsing.
NAHHAS:v1p220/r2.anchor: فعل مستقبل ( وتنسون ) عطف عليه ( أفلا تعقلون ) مثله

MUQATIL:2:44-46/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:44-46/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:44-46/r1.claim: Jews told some of Muhammad's companions that Muhammad was true and urged them to follow him, yet the Jews themselves left their own selves by not following him.
MUQATIL:2:44-46/r1.anchor: إن محمدا حق فاتبعوه ترشدوا، فقال الله عز وجل لليهود

MUQATIL:2:44-46/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:44-46/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:44-46/r2.claim: The Torah contains a clear account and description of Muhammad, so the Jews should understand and follow him.
MUQATIL:2:44-46/r2.anchor: يعنى التوراة فيها بيان أمر محمد ونعته،

ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r1.claim: The opening hamza in “a-taʾmurūna” is an interrogative used here to affirm and rebuke, as if telling them, “You are following this course.”
ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r1.anchor: فالألف ألف استفهام، ومعناه: التقرير والتوبيخ ههنا، كأنه قيل لهم: أنتم على هذه الطريقة.

ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r2.claim: The primary explanation is that they urged their followers to adhere to scripture while neglecting it themselves by rejecting the Prophet.
ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r2.anchor: أنهم كانوا يأمرون أتباعهم بالتمسك بكتابهم ويتركون هم التمسك به، لأن جحدهم النبي

ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r3.claim: Another possible explanation is that they urged almsgiving while withholding it themselves; this fits their hard hearts, usury, and illicit earnings, and withholding charity belongs to that pattern.
ZAJJAJ:v1p125/r3.anchor: ويجوز والله أعلم - أنهم كانوا يأمرون ببذل الصدقة وكانوا يضنون بها، لأنهم وصفوا بأنهم قست قلوبهم

THALABI:v1p188/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p188/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p188/r3.claim: The rebuke addresses those who command obedience and good works while neglecting them themselves; ‘Will you not reason?’ means will you not stop yourselves from this ruinous behavior.
THALABI:v1p188/r3.anchor: أتأمرون الناس بالبر الطاعة والعمل الصالح، وتنسون أنفسكم تتركون وأنتم تتلون الكتاب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r1.claim: Jews told their Muslim relatives to remain as they were, while they themselves would not believe; the verse rebukes them for urging belief in Muhammad but neglecting themselves.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r1.anchor: كانت اليهود تقول لأقربائهم من المسلمين: اثبتوا على ما أنتم عليه، ولا يؤمنون به،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r2.claim: The Book they recited was the Torah, which describes Muhammad; they should recognize its truth and follow it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:44-45/r2.anchor: تقرؤون التوراة وفيها صفة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ونعته

STUDYQURAN:2:44/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r1.claim: Depending on context, birr can mean goodness, kindness, loyalty, sincerity, or obedience; it is rendered here as piety.
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r1.anchor: Depending on context, the term rendered piety

STUDYQURAN:2:44/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r2.claim: The Quran discusses piety also at 2:177, 2:189, and 3:92.

STUDYQURAN:2:44/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r3.claim: The abrār (“pious”) are often associated with heavenly rewards.
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r3.anchor: are often mentioned in connection with heavenly rewards

STUDYQURAN:2:44/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r4.claim: Here piety can mean obedience to God, prayer, and almsgiving.
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r4.anchor: Piety in this verse can mean obedience to God as well as prayer and alms.

STUDYQURAN:2:44/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r5.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r5.claim: Some take the piety enjoined as acknowledgment of the Prophet's mission or as the earlier warning to the Arabs that a prophet would be sent among them.
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r5.anchor: Some mention that it could refer to acknowledgment of the Prophet’s mission or to the previous warning to the Arabs

STUDYQURAN:2:44/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r6.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:44/r6.claim: The verb rendered “recite” can also mean “study.”

TAB-FULL:v1p614/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says obedience is birr, as the reports describe the people as ordering obedience, piety, and righteousness.
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r1.anchor: كان بنو إسرائيل يأمرون الناس بطاعة الله وبتقواه وبالبر ويخالفون

TAB-FULL:v1p614/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r2.claim: They told people to reject disbelief based on the Torah's prophecy and covenant, yet rejected the covenant to affirm the Messenger and denied what they knew from Scripture.
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم وأنتم تتلون الكتاب أفلا تعقلون} [البقرة: 44] أي تنهون الناس عن الكفر

TAB-FULL:v1p614/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r3.claim: In a report through al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn Abbas says they urged people to enter Muhammad's religion and fulfill commands such as prayer, while neglecting themselves.
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: " في قوله: {أتأمرون الناس بالبر} [البقرة: 44] يقول: أتأمرون الناس بالدخول في دين محمد

TAB-FULL:v1p614/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r4.claim: They urged people to obey and fear God while themselves disobeying Him.
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r4.anchor: عن السدي: " {أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم} [البقرة: 44] قال: كانوا يأمرون الناس بطاعة الله وبتقواه وهم يعصونه

TAB-FULL:v1p614/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r5.claim: The Children of Israel ordered obedience, piety, and righteousness but acted against what they preached, so God reproached them.
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r5.anchor: عن قتادة: " في قوله: {أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم} [البقرة: 44] قال: كان بنو إسرائيل يأمرون الناس بطاعة الله

TAB-FULL:v1p614/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r6.claim: The People of Scripture and hypocrites told others to fast and pray but did not act on their commands.
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r6.anchor: قال ابن جريج: " {أتأمرون الناس بالبر} [البقرة: 44] أهل الكتاب والمنافقون كانوا يأمرون الناس بالصوم والصلاة

TAB-FULL:v1p614/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj adds the general lesson that whoever orders good should be the quickest to practice it.
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r7.anchor: فمن أمر بخير فليكن أشد الناس فيه مسارعة

TAB-FULL:v1p614/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says Jews would advise a questioner to act justly when the matter involved no right, bribe, or other personal stake.
TAB-FULL:v1p614/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " هؤلاء اليهود كان إذا جاء الرجل يسألهم ما ليس فيه حق ولا رشوة

TAB-FULL:v1p616/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p616/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء
TAB-FULL:v1p616/r1.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ says full understanding requires disliking people for God's sake, then turning to oneself with even stronger disapproval.
TAB-FULL:v1p616/r1.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء: لا يفقه الرجل كل الفقه حتى يمقت الناس في ذات الله

TAB-FULL:v1p616/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p616/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p616/r2.claim: The reported views differ over which good acts were meant, but all agree that the people urged others toward what pleases God in word or deed while acting otherwise themselves.
TAB-FULL:v1p616/r2.anchor: متفقون في أنهم كانوا يأمرون الناس بما لله فيه رضا من القول أو العمل

TAB-FULL:v1p616/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p616/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p616/r3.claim: The verse reproaches them for ordering others to obey God while leaving themselves to sin, asking why they do not command themselves as they command others.
TAB-FULL:v1p616/r3.anchor: فالتأويل الذي يدل على صحته ظاهر التلاوة إذا: أتأمرون الناس بطاعة الله وتتركون أنفسكم تعصيه، فهلا تأمرونها بما تأمرون به الناس من طاعة ربكم.

TAB-FULL:v1p616/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p616/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p616/r4.claim: Forgetting oneself here means abandoning obedience, as in the statement that they forgot God, meaning they left His obedience and God left them from His reward.
TAB-FULL:v1p616/r4.anchor: نظير النسيان الذي قال جل ثناؤه: {نسوا الله فنسيهم} [التوبة: 67] بمعنى: تركوا طاعة الله فتركهم الله من ثوابه

TAB-FULL:v1p616#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p616#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p616#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī glosses tatlūna as studying and reciting the Book; Ibn Abbas also reports that the phrase means studying the Torah.
TAB-FULL:v1p616#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {وأنتم تتلون الكتاب} [البقرة: 44] يقول: تدرسون الكتاب بذلك

TAB-FULL:v1p616#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p616#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p616#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as studying the Book and identifies the Book as the Torah.
TAB-FULL:v1p616#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {وأنتم تتلون الكتاب} [البقرة: 44] يقول: تدرسون الكتاب بذلك. ويعني بالكتاب: التوراة

TAB-FULL:v1p616#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p616#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p616#3/r1.claim: The question rebukes people for opposing what they teach, though they know their duty to obey God and follow Muhammad.
TAB-FULL:v1p616#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {أفلا تعقلون} [البقرة: 44] يقول: أفلا تفهمون فنهاهم عن هذا الخلق القبيح

TAB-FULL:v1p616#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p616#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p616#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the question as 'Do you not understand?' and says it rebukes this ugly behavior.
TAB-FULL:v1p616#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {أفلا تعقلون} [البقرة: 44] يقول: أفلا تفهمون فنهاهم عن هذا الخلق القبيح

TAB-FULL:v1p616#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p616#3/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p616#3/r3.claim: This supports that Israel's scholars urged others to follow Muhammad while claiming he had been sent to other people, not to them.
TAB-FULL:v1p616#3/r3.anchor: وهذا يدل على صحة ما قلنا من أمر أحبار يهود بني إسرائيل غيرهم باتباع محمد

TAB-FULL:v2p151#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p151#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p151#2/r1.claim: The rebuke reports Jewish leaders' warning to their own brethren not to tell the Prophet's Companions what Scripture said about him, since it would become evidence against them; God answers that He knows what they hide and reveal.
TAB-FULL:v2p151#2/r1.anchor: مبعوث حجة لهم عليكم عند ربكم يحتجون بها عليكم؟ أي فلا تفعلوا ذلك

TABRISI:2:44/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44/r1.claim: البر means goodness, kindness, or connection, opposite عقوق; forms برّ, بارّ, and بِرّ are used for charity and pilgrimage.
TABRISI:2:44/r1.anchor: البر في اللغة والإحسان والصلة نظائر يقال فلان بار وصول محسن وضد البر العقوق

TABRISI:2:44/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r2.speaker: الأخفش
TABRISI:2:44/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash explains “does not know the cat from the mouse” as failing to distinguish who hisses at a person from who treats him kindly.
TABRISI:2:44/r2.anchor: قال الأخفش: معناه لا يعرف من يهر عليه ممن يبره

TABRISI:2:44/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r3.speaker: المازني
TABRISI:2:44/r3.claim: Al-Māzinī says الهر is a cat and البر a mouse or similar small creature.
TABRISI:2:44/r3.anchor: وقال المازني: الهر السنور والبر الفأرة أو دويبة تشبهها

TABRISI:2:44/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44/r4.claim: البر differs from الخير because it implies intention, whereas good may happen accidentally or through forgetfulness.
TABRISI:2:44/r4.anchor: والفرق بين البر والخير أن البر يدل على قصد والخير قد يقع على وجه السهو

TABRISI:2:44/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44/r5.claim: Sahw and heedlessness are near-synonyms; forgetfulness is a necessary loss of something from the self after it was present, created by God.
TABRISI:2:44/r5.anchor: والسهو والغفلة نظائر وضد النسيان الذكر وحقيقته غروب الشيء عن النفس بعد حضوره

TABRISI:2:44/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44/r6.claim: Sahw can concern something a person knew or something previously unknown.
TABRISI:2:44/r6.anchor: والسهو قد يقع عما كان الإنسان عالما به وعما لم يكن عالما به

TABRISI:2:44/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44/r7.claim: نسيان can mean neglecting or abandoning, as in “they forgot God and He forgot them,” meaning He left them without aid.

TABRISI:2:44/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44/r8.claim: تلاوة can mean recitation or following; its original sense is following because each letter follows the one before it.
TABRISI:2:44/r8.anchor: والتلاوة القراءة تلا يتلو تلاوة أي قرأ وتلا يتلو تلوا أي تبع

TABRISI:2:44/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44/r9.claim: Reading originally gathers letters, while recitation follows letters in sequence.
TABRISI:2:44/r9.anchor: والفرق بين التلاوة والقراءة أن أصل القراءة جمع الحروف وأصل التلاوة اتباع الحروف

TABRISI:2:44/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44/r10.claim: Intellect, understanding, recognition, and discernment are near-synonyms; its opposite is foolishness.
TABRISI:2:44/r10.anchor: والعقل والفهم والمعرفة واللب نظائر ورجل عاقل فهم لبيب ذو معرفة وضد العقل الحمق

TABRISI:2:44/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:44/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās attributes his learning to “a discerning heart and a questioning tongue.”
TABRISI:2:44/r11.anchor: وقيل لابن عباس: أنى لك هذا العلم؟

TABRISI:2:44/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r12.speaker: صاحب كتاب العين
TABRISI:2:44/r12.claim: The author of Kitāb al-ʿAyn treats intellect as the opposite of ignorance, with usages for becoming informed or regaining one’s senses after delirium.
TABRISI:2:44/r12.anchor: وقال صاحب كتاب العين: العقل ضد الجهل

TABRISI:2:44/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44/r13.claim: عقال is a tether: عقلت البعير means tying a camel’s leg with its hobble.
TABRISI:2:44/r13.anchor: والعقال الرباط يقال عقلت البعير أعقله عقلا إذا شددت يده بالعقال

TABRISI:2:44/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44/r14.claim: Intellect is knowledge that restrains a living being from reprehensible acts and prompts obligations; it is not predicated of God, who needs no restraint and acquires no knowledge.
TABRISI:2:44/r14.anchor: والعقل مجموع علوم لأجلها يمتنع الحي من كثير من المقبحات ويفعل كثيرا من الواجبات

TABRISI:2:44/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r15.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:2:44/r15.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā defines intellect as knowledge that restrains one from evil; the stronger its restraint, the more intelligent its possessor.
TABRISI:2:44/r15.anchor: وقال علي بن عيسى: العقل هو العلم الذي يزجر عن قبيح الفعل

TABRISI:2:44/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r16.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:44/r16.claim: Other definitions call intellect the general ability to distinguish good from bad, or the faculty distinguishing humans from animals; al-Ṭabrisī says they are close.
TABRISI:2:44/r16.anchor: وقيل العقل معرفة يفصل بها بين القبيح والحسن في الجملة

TABRISI:2:44/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44/r17.claim: Intellect can be complete despite missing some knowledge, while knowledge cannot be complete if some intellect is absent.
TABRISI:2:44/r17.anchor: والفرق بين العقل والعلم أن العقل قد يكمل لمن فقد بعض العلوم

TABRISI:2:44/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44/r18.claim: Disagreement over intellect’s essence does not alter rational judgments such as one hundred being greater than one or the whole greater than its part.
TABRISI:2:44/r18.anchor: إن الاختلاف في ماهية العقل لا يوجب الاختلاف في قضاياه

TABRISI:2:44#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44#2/r1.claim: The address targets Jewish scholars who told Muslim relatives to remain in their faith while they themselves did not believe; the opening alif is an interrogative rebuke.
TABRISI:2:44#2/r1.anchor: هذه الآية خطاب لعلماء اليهود وكانوا يقولون لأقربائهم من المسلمين اثبتوا على ما أنتم عليه

TABRISI:2:44#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44#2/r2.claim: Here البر is belief in Muḥammad; God rebukes them for telling people to believe in him while withholding belief themselves.
TABRISI:2:44#2/r2.anchor: والمراد بالبر الإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وبخهم الله تعالى على ما كانوا يفعلون

TABRISI:2:44#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44#2/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:2:44#2/r3.claim: Abū Muslim says they told Arabs to believe in Muḥammad when he was sent, but disbelieved once he came.
TABRISI:2:44#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: كانوا يأمرون العرب بالإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا بعث

TABRISI:2:44#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:44#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they urged followers to adhere to the Torah but failed themselves, since denying the Prophet and his description in it abandoned the Torah.
TABRISI:2:44#2/r4.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أن المراد أنهم كانوا يأمرون أتباعهم بالتمسك بالتوراة

TABRISI:2:44#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:2:44#2/r5.claim: Qatāda says they commanded people to obey God while disobeying Him themselves.
TABRISI:2:44#2/r5.anchor: وعن قتادة كانوا يأمرون الناس بطاعة الله وهم يخالفونه

TABRISI:2:44#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44#2/r6.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TABRISI:2:44#2/r6.claim: Anas ibn Mālik reports the Prophet’s Night Journey account: Gabriel identifies people whose lips are cut with fiery scissors as worldly preachers who urge goodness but forget themselves.
TABRISI:2:44#2/r6.anchor: وروى أنس بن مالك قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

TABRISI:2:44#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TABRISI:2:44#2/r7.claim: Another reported interpretation says they urged charity but withheld it and embezzled donations entrusted for the poor.
TABRISI:2:44#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم أتأمرون الناس بالصدقة وتتركونها وإذا أتتكم الضعفاء بالصدقة

TABRISI:2:44#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:44#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Book they recited was the Torah, which contains the Prophet’s description.
TABRISI:2:44#2/r8.anchor: معناه وأنتم تقرأون التوراة وفيها صفته ونعته عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:2:44#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44#2/r9.claim: The rebuke may mean: do you not understand that your conduct is irrational and morally ugly?
TABRISI:2:44#2/r9.anchor: أفلا تفقهون أن ما تفعلونه قبيح في العقول

TABRISI:2:44#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44#2/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:2:44#2/r10.claim: Abū Muslim glosses the question as saying this is not the conduct of a rational person.
TABRISI:2:44#2/r10.anchor: وعن أبي مسلم أن معناه هذا ليس بفعل من يعقل

TABRISI:2:44#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44#2/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:44#2/r11.claim: Other glosses ask whether they know God will punish them, or know the Torah is true and therefore should affirm and follow Muḥammad.
TABRISI:2:44#2/r11.anchor: وقيل معناه أفلا تعلمون أن الله يعذبكم ويعاقبكم على ذلك

TABRISI:2:44#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44#2/r12.claim: God does not rebuke them for commanding goodness; He rebukes their abandoning it themselves, a worse failure in someone who teaches it.
TABRISI:2:44#2/r12.anchor: لم يوبخهم الله على الأمر بالبر وإنما وبخهم على ترك فعل البر المضموم إلى الأمر بالبر

TABRISI:2:44#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44#2/r13.claim: The poet’s maxim condemns committing the vice one forbids; it does not forbid warning others against bad conduct.
TABRISI:2:44#2/r13.anchor: لا تنه عن خلق وتأتي مثله عار عليك إذا فعلت عظيم

TABRISI:2:44#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:44#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:44#3/r1.claim: The continuation clarifies that the poem does not prohibit forbidding vice; it prohibits committing the same vice oneself.
TABRISI:2:44#3/r1.anchor: ومعلوم أنه لم يرد به النهي عن الخلق المذموم وإنما أراد النهي عن إتيان مثله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r1.claim: The verse was revealed about Jewish scholars who told Muslim relatives to remain in their faith while they themselves refused to believe.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r1.anchor: نزلت في علماء اليهود، لأنهم كانوا يقولون لأقربائهم من المسلمين: اثبتوا على ما أنتم عليه، ولا يؤمنون (¬3).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r2.claim: The initial hamza is interrogative, conveying rebuke and threat, as if telling them that this is the path they follow.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r2.anchor: و (الألف) للاستفهام (¬4)، ومعناه: التوبيخ والتهديد (¬5)، كأنه قيل لهم: أنتم على هذه الطريقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r3.claim: Here birr means faith in Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r3.anchor: والمراد بالبر: الإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم (¬1).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r4.claim: Nisyan here means abandoning; the author points to 9:67 and promises a fuller discussion at the cited 2:67.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r4.anchor: و (النسيان) هاهنا بمعنى الترك (¬2) من قوله: {نسوا الله فنسيهم} [التوبة: 67]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq says they urged their followers to adhere to their scripture but abandoned it themselves by denying the Prophet; on this reading birr means holding to the Torah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r5.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: معنى الآية أنهم كانوا يأمرون أتباعهم بالتمسك بكتابهم، ويتركون هم التمسك به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r6.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r6.claim: Some say the Jews urged people to believe in Muhammad before his appearance, then disbelieved in him once he appeared.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p448/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إن اليهود كانوا يأمرون الناس بالإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل ظهوره، فلما ظهر كفروا به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r1.claim: They read the Torah, which contains Muhammad's description and attributes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r1.anchor: أي: تقرؤون التوراة، وفيها صفة محمد -صلى الله عليه وسلم- ونعته (¬6).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r2.claim: The rhetorical question asks why they do not recognize that Muhammad is true and follow him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r3.claim: Tilawa comes from tala-yatlu, to follow; recitation is called following the letters.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r3.anchor: وأصل التلاوة من قولهم: تلاه يتلوه، إذا تبعه، والتلاوة اتباع الحروف (¬1).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r4.claim: Intellect distinguishes humans from animals and is named for restraining a person from ruin, as a camel's hobble keeps it from running off; diya is called ʿaql because payment restrains a victim's guardian from killing the offender.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r4.anchor: سمي عقلا لأنه يعقله أي يمنعه عن التورط (¬3) في الهلكة، كما يعقل العقال البعير عن ركوب رأسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r5.claim: Al-Asmaʿi gives related usages: a gazelle ʿaqala when it holds back, an ibex is called ʿaqil, a fortress maʿqil, and medicine ʿaqala the stomach when it stops diarrhea.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r5.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: عقل الظبي يعقل عقولا، إذا امتنع، ومنه سمى الوعل عاقلا، والحصن معقلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r6.claim: The root sense is restraint; because a person knows things through intellect, ʿaql can also mean knowledge, as in ʿaqaltu hadha, I knew this.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p449/r6.anchor: فأصل هذا الحرف من المنع، ثم لما كان الإنسان يعرف الشيء بعقله، سمي العلم عقلا في (¬7) بعض المواضع

QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r7.claim: The rebuke asks why people urge others to hasten toward God while lagging themselves, dispatch visitors without arriving, or press others in spiritual states while lacking outward practice.
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r7.anchor: أتحرضون الناس على البدار وترضون بالتخلف

QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r8.claim: They scrutinize a speck of truth and a measure of love in others yet allot themselves heaps of faults like sand and mountains.
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r8.anchor: أتبصرون من الحق مثقال الذر ومقياس الحب

QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r9.speaker: أنشدوا
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r9.claim: An anonymous poem depicts seeing a mote in another’s eye while failing to see a log in one’s own.
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r9.anchor: قال قائلهم : وتبصر في العين مني القذى

QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r10.claim: The author adds a cryptic rebuke asking whether they water others with fine camels but do not drink by turns.
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r10.anchor: ويقال أتسقون بالنجب ولا تشربون بالنوب

QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r11.claim: Despite reciting scripture, they resist with hidden claims and deny the disclosures of thought and clear inner warnings that have touched their hearts.
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r11.anchor: ثم تعاندون بخافايا الدعاوى وتجحدون بما شام قلوبكم

QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r12.claim: The conduct just described is a blameworthy trait and ugly action.
QUSHAYRI:v1p42/r12.anchor: إن ذلك ذميم من الخصال وقبيح من الفعال

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r1.claim: Birr literally means goodness and rightness; as a religious and ethical term it spans faith, worship, all forms of goodness and beneficence, obedience, uprightness, and sinlessness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r1.anchor: Sözlükte “iyilik, doğruluk” anlamına gelen birr kelimesinin, dinî ve ahlâkî bir terim olarak, iman ve ibadetten başlamak üzere

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r2.claim: For further discussion of birr, the commentary refers to 2:177 and 3:92.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r2.anchor: (ayrıntılı bilgi için bk. Bakara 2/ 177; Âl-i İmrân 3/92).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r3.claim: The verse's immediate addressees are Jewish religious scholars, who urged people to believe in and practice the sacred book and live by God's approval in word and deed, while their own conduct contradicted their teaching and eroded sincere religiosity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r3.anchor: Bu âyetten, asıl muhatapların yahudi din bilginleri olduğu anlaşılmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r4.claim: The question about reason indicates that the scholars' contradiction violates not only religious rulings but also rational judgment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r4.anchor: bu çelişkili tutumlarının, yalnızca dinin hükümlerine değil, akla da aykırı olduğuna işaret etmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r5.claim: The criticism of Jewish scholars' insincerity also warns the Muslim community, especially religious leaders and scholars: preaching goodness while acting against it violates a universal ethic of word-deed integrity rejected by the Quran.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r5.anchor: bir yandan da genel olarak İslâm ümmeti, özellikle müslüman din önderleri ve bilginleri için de bir uyarı anlamı taşımaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r6.claim: The same warning is stated in 61:2–3, where believers are rebuked for saying what they do not do.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:44/r6.anchor: Nitekim Saf sûresinde “Ey iman edenler! Yapmayacağınız şeyleri niye söylersiniz? Yapmayacağınız şeyleri söylemeniz Allah katında çok sevimsiz bir davranıştır!” (61/2-3) buyurulmaktadır.

BURHAN:v3p354/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.claim: The four broken plural forms of paucity and the two sound plurals are inherently paucity forms; other plurals may indicate few or many as context determines, as Qur'anic examples show.
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.anchor: واعلم أن جموع التكثير الأربعة وجمعى التصحيح أعنى جمع التأنيث وجمع التذكير كل ذلك للقلة

BURHAN:v3p164/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p164/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p164/r9.claim: Objects are often omitted at verse endings, including “while you know” and “while you recite the Book”; omission asserts the verb for its subject without restricting its object.
BURHAN:v3p164/r9.anchor: وكثيرا ما يعترى الحذف في رءوس الآى نحو

BURHAN:v4p436/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p436/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p436/r5.claim: Resumptive coordination and circumstantial waw occur together, as in “while you know,” “while you recite the Book,” and the other cited clauses.
BURHAN:v4p436/r5.anchor: وقد يجتمعان نحو ﴿ فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا وأنتم تعلمون ﴾

BURHAN:v1p83/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p83/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p83/r3.claim: The ending أفلا تعقلون occurs in a context that condemns conduct contrary to reason, since its perpetrator is not acting rationally.
BURHAN:v1p83/r3.anchor: وهذه الفاصلة لا تقع إلا فى سياق إنكار فعل غير مناسب فى العقل

BURHAN:v3p372/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p372/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p372/r4.claim: He glosses وإذ قال الله as يقول; the present tense in أتأمرون وتنسون conveys continuing, recurrent conduct.
BURHAN:v3p372/r4.anchor: لأن المضارع يراد به الديمومة والاستمرار كقوله ﴿ أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم

SULAMI:v1p59#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p59#2/r1.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p59#2/r1.claim: The reproach is read as demanding from people the realities of spiritual meanings while lacking their outward observance oneself.
SULAMI:v1p59#2/r1.anchor: قيل فيه : أتطالبون الناس بحقائق المعاني وأنتم خالون من ظاهر رسومها

ITQAN:v3p105/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p105/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p105/r1.claim: Present-tense forms can describe past conduct as ongoing and persistent; ‘you command people to goodness and forget yourselves’ is an example.
ITQAN:v3p105/r1.anchor: وعكسه لإفادة الدوام والإستمرار فكأنه وقع واستمر نحو ﴿ أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون ﴾

ITQAN:v3p214/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p214/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v3p214/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the interrogative hamza in 2:44 combines affirmation, rebuke, and astonishment at their conduct.
ITQAN:v3p214/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري الهمزة للتقرير مع التوبيخ والتعجب من حالهم

ITQAN:v3p218/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p218/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p218/r3.claim: The hamza rule is harder in 2:44: commanding goodness is not blameworthy, forgetting oneself is, and neither combining them nor making forgetfulness conditional on teaching fully explains the wording.
ITQAN:v3p218/r3.anchor: وأشكل منه قوله ﴿ أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم ﴾ ووجه الإشكال

ITQAN:v3p218/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p218/r4.speaker: عروس الأفراح
ITQAN:v3p218/r4.claim: ‘Arous al-Afrah answers that sinning while forbidding the same sin is worse because conduct contradicts speech, and sin with knowledge is graver; the author says the difficulty remains subtle.
ITQAN:v3p218/r4.anchor: قال في عروس الأفراح ويجاب بأن فعل المعصية مع النهي عنها أفحش لأنها تجعل حال الإنسان كالمتناقض

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r1.claim: The Qur'anic challenge must name a quality the challenged audience can recognize; otherwise neither a valid demand nor proof of incapacity exists.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r1.anchor: مطالبة بأن يأتوا بكلام على وصف ولا تصح المطالبة بالإتيان به على وصف من غير أن يكون ذلك الوصف معلوما للمطالب

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r2.claim: The ring analogy shows that inability cannot be established until the claimed craft is shown and the other person tries to produce that known thing.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r2.anchor: لأنه لا يصح وصف الإنسان بأنه قد عجز عن شيء حتى يريد ذلك الشيء

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r3.claim: The Qur'an's distinguishing quality cannot lie in individual words or their ordinary lexical meanings, since these existed before its revelation.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r3.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون في الكلم المفردة لأن تقدير كونه فيها يؤدي إلى المحال

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r4.claim: The challenge is not merely to reproduce Qur'anic sound sequences or meter; that reduction would make the challenge as absurd as Musaylima's imitations.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p289/r4.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون هذا الوصف في تركيب الحركات والسكنات حتى كأنهم تحدوا إلى أن يأتوا بكلام تكون كلماته على تواليها في زنة كلمات القرآن

TUSTARI:2:44/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:44/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:44/r1.claim: The Jews urged their foster brothers to obey God and follow the Prophet while failing to do so themselves.
TUSTARI:2:44/r1.anchor: يعني اليهود كانوا يأمرون إخوانهم من الرضاعة بطاعة الله تعالى واتباع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p19/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p19/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p19/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse addressed Medinan Jews who urged Muslim relatives and in-laws to remain in their faith and follow the Prophet, though they did not practice that advice.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p19/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال نزلت هذه الآية في يهود أهل المدينة

DAMGHANI:v1p67/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p67/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p67/r6.claim: Birr means taqwā, obedience to God and following Muhammad.
DAMGHANI:v1p67/r6.anchor: يعني بالتقوى أي طاعة الله تعالى وإتباع محمد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r1.claim: In origin, al-birr names what brings benefit to the person receiving someone's kindness.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r1.anchor: البر في الأصل : اسم لما يحصل به للمبرور النفع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r2.claim: Ibn Faris gives birr as the opposite of disobedience and as truth; the entry also notes obedience to one's Lord, superiority over one's peers, arak fruit, and excessive talk as related forms.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r2.anchor: قال ابن فارس : والبر : ضد العقوق . والبر : الصدق .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r3.claim: The first Qur'anic sense is maintaining kinship, in commands to be righteous toward relatives and just toward non-hostile people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r3.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن البر في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r4.claim: The second sense is obedience, illustrated by cooperation in righteousness, dutifulness to parents, righteous conversation, and the record and character of the righteous angels.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن البر في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r5.claim: The third Qur'anic sense is piety, including the rebuke for commanding others to be righteous while neglecting oneself and the description of true righteousness.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p190/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن البر في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#2/r1.claim: Forgetting yourselves means abandoning yourselves, as in 9:67, where forgetting God means leaving Him and being left by Him.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p47#2/r1.anchor: وتنسون أنفسكم} أي: وتتركون أنفسكم، كما قال: {نسوا الله فنسيهم} (1) أي: تركوا الله فتركهم.

SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r1.claim: The hamza expresses denial and reproach, or wonder at their state.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r1.anchor: الهمزة للإنكار والتوبيخ أو للتعجب من حالهم

SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r2.claim: أمر governs two complements, one directly and one by a preposition, though one may be omitted; الناس is first, بالبر second, as in the poem امرتك الخير and ما أمرت به.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r2.anchor: فالناس مفعول أول، وبالبر مفعول ثان

SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r3.claim: البر means expansive goodness, including kinship and obedience; البر and البرية are associated with spaciousness.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r3.anchor: والبر: سعة الخير من الصلة والطاعة، ومنه البر والبرية لسعتهما

SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r4.claim: The verb بَرِيبر follows فَعِلَ يَفعل; the poem's يبرك الناس means they obey You.

SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r5.claim: البر also means fox cub or driving sheep; لا يعرف الهر من البر distinguishes a cat's call from sheep-driving.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r5.anchor: والبر أيضا: ولد الثعلب وسوق الغنم

SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r6.claim: البر can also mean the heart, as in the poet's أكون مكان البر منه.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r6.anchor: والبر أيضا الفؤاد، قال: 425 أكون مكان البر منه ودونه

SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r7.claim: With fatḥa, البر means reverence and honor; a dutiful son honors parents, and God is al-Barr because His goodness is expansive.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r7.anchor: والبر بالفتح الإجلال والتعظيم، ومنه: ولد بر بوالديه

SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r8.claim: تنسون lies within the reproach; its underlying form is تنسيون, with yāʾ deleted after becoming quiescent, giving تفعون, as in the earlier discussion of اشتروا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r8.anchor: وأصل تنسون: تنسيون، فأعل بحذف الياء سكونها

SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r9.claim: نسيان is the opposite of remembering and usually a lapse after knowledge, but can mean neglect or abandon, as in نسوا الله فنسيهم.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r9.anchor: والنسيان: ضد الذكر، وهو السهو الحاصل بعد حصول العلم، وقد يطلق على الترك

SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r10.claim: The verb can take تعليق by analogy with its opposite; the poem's نسينا من أنتم illustrates it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44/r10.anchor: وقد يدخله التعليق حملا على نقيضه

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r1.speaker: author
