SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r1.claim: وأنتم تتلون الكتاب is a subject-predicate clause in the accusative as حال, governed by تنسون.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r1.anchor: مبتدأ وخبر في محل نصب على الحال، العامل فيها " تنسون "

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r2.claim: تلاوة means following in sequence; recitation is so called because words follow one another, as the moon follows the sun in the cited verse.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r2.anchor: والتلاوة: التتابع، ومنه تلاوة القرآن، لأن القارئ يتبع كلماته بعضها ببعض

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r3.claim: The underlying form is تتلوون with two wāws; the first wāw's heavy ḍamma is dropped, then a quiescent letter is deleted, yielding تفعون.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r3.anchor: وأصل تتلون: تتلوون بواوين فاستثقلت الضمة على الواو الأولى

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r4.claim: The hamza in أفلا تعقلون expresses denial.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r4.anchor: الهمزة للإنكار أيضا، وهي في نية التأخير عن الفاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r5.claim: The hamza is understood as delayed until after فاء; it may precede wāw and thumma, as in 2:77 and 10:51, but not other conjunctions, according to most grammarians.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r5.anchor: وهي في نية التأخير عن الفاء لأنها حرف عطف، وكذا تتقدم أيضا على الواو وثم

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī places the hamza where it appears and supplies a verb before the conjunction; al-Samīn notes qualified disagreement with this rule.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r6.anchor: وزعم الزمخشري أن الهمزة في موضعها غير منوي بها التأخير، ويقدر قبل الفاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r7.claim: The object of تعقلون is unexpressed, either meaning whether they have reason or recognize the ugliness of their conduct.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r7.anchor: ومفعول " تعقلون " غير مراد، لأن المعنى: أفلا يكون منكم [عقل]

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r8.claim: العقل is perception that prevents error; its basic sense is restraint, as with a camel's hobble and blood money that restrains killing.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r8.anchor: والعقل: الإدراك المانع من الخطأ، وأصله المنع

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r9.claim: العقل also means an embroidered garment; ʿAlqama's عقلا witnesses it, and Ibn Fāris distinguishes linear ornament عقل from circular رقم.
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r9.anchor: قال علقمة: 427 عقلا ورقما تظل الطير تتبعه

SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:44#2/r10.claim: The interrogative clause has no syntactic position because it is independent.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#2/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#2/r7.claim: Al-Baqara places prostration before the word of repentance because prostration is nobler and follows the preceding prayer and bowing passage, including 2:44; al-Aʿrāf omits that sequence and delays prostration.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#2/r7.anchor: لأن السجود أشرف من القول لأنه أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد

NASHR:v1p223/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p223/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p223/r1.claim: Nūn is more inherently nasal than mīm because it is closer to the nasal cavity; reciters should avoid over-darkening it, especially when vowelled after alif, and articulate it at pause.
NASHR:v1p223/r1.anchor: والنون: حرف أغن آصل في الغنة من الميم لقربه من الخيشوم

NASHR:v1p223/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p223/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p223/r2.claim: Hāʾ needs careful articulation because it is remote and faint; preserve it in neighboring and geminated contexts, including when written twice but pronounced once.
NASHR:v1p223/r2.anchor: والهاء: يعتنى بها مخرجا وصفة لبعدها وخفائها فكم من مقصر فيها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p44#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p44#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p44#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says the Children of Israel urged people to obey God, fear Him, and do good while acting contrary to that themselves, so God reproached them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p44#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم ﴾ قال كان بنوا إسرائيل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r1.claim: After commanding good as gratitude for their special favors, God urges them from another angle.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r1.anchor: ثم أنه تعالى لما أمرهم بفعل الخير شكرا لما خصهم به من النعم حرضهم على ذلك من مأخذ آخر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r2.claim: The interrogative hamza demands acknowledgment while expressing reproach and astonishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r2.anchor: والهمزة فيه للتقرير مع توبيخ وتعجيب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r3.claim: Birr is expansive goodness and includes every good; forgetting oneself means abandoning oneself as though forgotten, not literal forgetfulness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r3.anchor: والبرسعة المعروف والخير ومنه البر والبرية للسعة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the verse was revealed about Medina's Jewish scholars, who privately urged people to follow Muhammad but did not follow him themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r4.anchor: على ما روى عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما في أحبار المدينة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r5.claim: Another report says the scholars ordered people to give charity but did not give it themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : إنهم كانوا يأمرون بالصدقة ولا يتصدقون

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r6.claim: Birr may mean faith or beneficence; al-Suddī instead leaves it broad: they ordered obedience and prohibited disobedience while neglecting obedience and committing sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r6.anchor: فالمراد بالبر هنا إما الإيمان أو الإحسان وتركه بعضهم على ظاهره متناولا كل خير على ما قال السدي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r7.claim: The reproach targets not their instruction to do good, but combining it with neglect of their own conduct.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r8.claim: The book they recite is the Torah; the clause describes the speakers' state and intensifies the rebuke.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r8.anchor: الجملة حال من فاعل ( أتأمرون ) والمراد التبكيت وزيادة التقبيح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r9.claim: Most take the underlying order to place the conjunction before the hamza, which moves first because it begins the sentence; others posit no inversion and an omitted clause for coordination.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r9.anchor: أصل هذا الكلام ونحوه عند الجمهور كان بتقديم حرف العطف على الهمزة لكن لما كان للهمزة صدر الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r10.claim: ʿAql originally means restraint, like a camel's hobble; it names the spiritual light by which souls grasp necessary and theoretical knowledge and are restrained from vice.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r10.anchor: ومنه عقال البعير سمى به النور الروحاني الذي به تدرك النفوس العلوم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r11.claim: The verb may be intransitive or transitive with an omitted object: do you lack reason to avoid a bad outcome, or to recognize the legal and rational ugliness of this contradiction?
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r11.anchor: والفعل يحتمل أن يكون مطلقا أجرى مجرى اللازم ويحتمل أن يكون متعديا مقدرا لمفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r12.claim: This verse does not establish the Muʿtazilite doctrine of intrinsic rational moral wrongness; some scholars argue it supports the opposite because rebuke follows their recitation of scripture.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r12.anchor: فعلى هذا لا حجة للمعتزلة في الآية على القبح العقلي الذي يزعمونه بل قد ادعى بعض المحققين أنها دليل على خلاف ما ذهبوا إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r13.claim: The rebuke does not bar a sinner from commanding right and forbidding wrong; failing to forbid evil is one sin, and committing it is another.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r13.anchor: فإن ترك النهي ذنب وارتكابه ذنب آخر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r14.claim: Though addressed to the Children of Israel, the warning applies to every preacher who urges others to act but does not act, or forbids conduct he himself commits.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r14.anchor: وإن كان خطابا لبني إسرائيل إلا أنه عام من حيث المعنى لكل واعظ يأمر ولا يأتمر ويزجر ولا ينزجر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r15.speaker: محمد بن واسع
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r15.claim: Muḥammad ibn Wāsiʿ reports that people in Paradise will confront people in Hell who had advised them to do good but themselves acted otherwise.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r15.anchor: وعن محمد بن واسع قال : بلغني أن أناسا من أهل الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r16.claim: Some address the verse to believers and read the book as the Qurʾān, taking it as a shift in address like the cited speech to Joseph; the apparent sense weighs against this.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p247#2/r16.anchor: ومن الناس من جعل هذا الخطاب للمؤمنين وحمل الكتاب على القرآن فيكون ذلك من تلوين الخطاب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r1.claim: The question is a forceful assertion that rebukes and expresses astonishment.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r2.claim: Birr means breadth in doing good, from barr, an open expanse; it includes every good and comprises devotion to God, care for relatives, and kindness to strangers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r2.anchor: والبر: التوسع في الخير، من البر وهو الفضاء الواسع يتناول كل خير، ولذلك قيل ثلاثة:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r3.claim: Forgetting yourselves means leaving yourselves out of the good you urge on others, as though you were forgotten.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r3.anchor: وتنسون أنفسكم } وتتركونها من البر كالمنسيات،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed about learned rabbis in Medina who privately urged people they advised to follow Muḥammad but did not follow him themselves.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنها نزلت في أحبار المدينة، كانوا يأمرون سرا من نصحوه باتباع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا يتبعونه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r5.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r5.claim: Another explanation says they commanded almsgiving but did not give charity themselves.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r5.anchor: وقيل: كانوا يأمرون بالصدقة ولا يتصدقون

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r6.claim: The reminder that they recite Scripture censures them, like the phrase while you know; the Torah warns against stubbornness, abandoning good, and making practice contradict speech.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r6.anchor: تبكيت كقوله: { وأنتم تعلمون } أي تتلون التوراة، وفيها الوعيد على العناد وترك البر ومخالفة القول العمل.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r7.claim: The question may ask whether they perceive the ugliness of their conduct and so desist, or whether they lack the intellect to stop what they know has a bad outcome. ʿAql originally means restraint.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r7.anchor: قبح صنيعكم فيصدكم عنه، أو أفلا عقل لكم يمنعكم عما تعلمون وخامة عاقبته. والعقل في الأصل الحبس،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r8.claim: The verse condemns the preacher who does not practice his own counsel, urging self-purification so he can improve others; it does not forbid a sinner to preach, since failing one duty does not cancel another.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:44/r8.anchor: والآية ناعية على من يعظ غيره ولا يتعظ بنفسه سوء صنيعه وخبث نفسه، وأن فعله فعل الجاهل بالشرع

DURR-FULL:v1p155/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p155/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p155/r9.claim: Qatāda identifies the rebuked people as the People of the Book, who urged righteousness but forgot themselves and did not benefit from scripture.
DURR-FULL:v1p155/r9.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم} قال: أولئك أهل الكتاب كانوا يأمرون الناس بالبر وينسون أنفسهم

DURR-FULL:v1p155/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p155/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p155/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse concerned Jews of Medina urging Muslim relatives to remain on their religion and affirming Muhammad’s teaching, though they did not follow it themselves.
DURR-FULL:v1p155/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت هذه الآية في يهود أهل المدينة كان الرجل منهم يقول لصهره ولذوي قرابته

DURR-FULL:v1p155/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p155/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p155/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses righteousness here as entering Muhammad’s religion.
DURR-FULL:v1p155/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {أتأمرون الناس بالبر} قال: بالدخول في دين محمد

DURR-FULL:v1p155/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p155/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p155/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains reciting the Book as studying it in this regard.
DURR-FULL:v1p155/r12.anchor: وأنتم تتلون} يقولون: تدرسون الكتاب بذلك

DURR-FULL:v1p155/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p155/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p155/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the question as asking whether they understand, and says it forbids this ugly conduct.
DURR-FULL:v1p155/r13.anchor: أفلا تعقلون} تفهمون ينهاهم عن هذا الخلق القبيح

IBNABIHATIM:v1p100#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p100#2/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p100#2/r1.claim: Anas reports that during the Ascension the Prophet saw people whose lips were cut; Gabriel identified them as preachers who urge righteousness but neglect themselves and do not reason over scripture.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p100#2/r1.anchor: عن انس بن مالك قال : لما عرج بالنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم مر على قوم تقرض شفاههم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p100#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p100#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p100#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says they deny the covenant in their Book to affirm the Messenger, break God’s pact, and reject what they know from scripture.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p100#2/r2.anchor: به عن ابن عباس : وأنتم تتلون الكتاب افلا تعقلون ؟ اي تكفرون بما فيه من عهدي اليكم في تصديق رسولي

IBNABIHATIM:v1p100#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p100#2/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p100#2/r3.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd reports from his father that “will you not reason?” means “will you not reflect?”
IBNABIHATIM:v1p100#2/r3.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن اسلم عن أبيه في قوله : افلا تعقلون افلا تتفكرون .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p471/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p471/r4.speaker: الطيبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p471/r4.claim: Al-Ṭībī argues that taʿlamūn here is not intransitive for being generally knowledgeable, since the following question denies them reason; otherwise knowledge would be affirmed while intellect is denied.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p471/r4.anchor: قال الطيبي عند قوله تعالى الآتي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r1.claim: The clause “and you forget yourselves” may be circumstantial to “you command,” making the rebuke concern commanding while self-neglecting, or coordinated and itself the main object of blame.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r1.anchor: جملة : { وتنسون أنفسكم } يجوز أن تكون حالا من ضمير { تأمرون } أو يكون محل التوبيخ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r2.speaker: الفخر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects the inference attributed to al-Fakhr that a sinner may not enjoin good or forbid wrong: the verse censures a shameful state, not a prohibited act.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r2.anchor: كما نقل عنهم الفخر في ( التفسير ) فإنه ليس المقصود نهي ولا تحريم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r3.claim: Nafs can denote the whole human self, body and spirit; Arabic also uses it for a person’s whole being, as in self-reference and the cited verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r3.anchor: والأنفس جمع نفس بسكون الفاء وهي مجموع ذات الإنسان من الهيكل والروح كما هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r4.claim: Nafs can also mean a part or the inward consciousness: the commentator cites ordinary speech and Qur’anic examples for these uses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r4.anchor: وتارة على البعض كقول القائل أنكرت نفسي وقوله : { وتنسون أنفسكم } وعلى الإحساس الباطني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r5.claim: Nafs can denote the spirit responsible for perception; Ibn Ashur promises further explanation when discussing the verse about every soul on Judgment Day.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r5.anchor: وتطلق على الروح الذي به الإدراك { إن النفس لأمارة بالسوء } ( يوسف : 53 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r6.claim: Reciting the Torah makes self-neglect especially outrageous: both urging others to righteousness and reading its commands and prohibitions should remind the speaker to reform himself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p476/r6.anchor: لأن نسيان أنفسهم يكون أغرب وأفظع إذا كان معهم أمران يقلعانه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477/r1.claim: The question is an emphatic denial and rebuke, treating them as though reason had disappeared because they neglect themselves despite two reminders of their need to reform.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477/r1.anchor: استفهاما مستعملا في الإنكار والتوبيخ نزلوا منزلة من انتفى تعقله فأنكر عليهم ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477/r2.claim: The verb “reason” is treated as intransitive or is inherently intransitive here, underscoring their extreme heedlessness and disordered condition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p477/r2.anchor: وفعل { تعقلون } منزل منزلة اللازم أو هو لازم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about Jews who privately told Muslim relatives to remain firm because Islam was true.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس نزلت في اليهود كان الرجل يقول لقرابته من المسلمين في السر اثبت على ما أنت عليه فإنه حق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r2.claim: The initial hamza is interrogative and gives the question a reproachful force.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r2.anchor: والألف في أتأمرون ألف الاستفهام ومعناه التوبيخ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r3.claim: One Ibn Abbas interpretation takes birr as adhering to their scripture, which they urged others to follow without practicing it themselves.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r3.anchor: أحدها أنه التمسك بكتابهم كانوا يأمرون باتباعه ولا يقومون به والثاني اتباع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم روي القولان عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r4.claim: Another Ibn Abbas interpretation takes birr as following Muhammad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r4.anchor: والثاني اتباع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم روي القولان عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says birr here means charity, which they urged while being miserly themselves.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r5.anchor: والثالث الصدقة كانوا يأمرون بها ويبخلون ذكره الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r6.anchor: أي تتركون وفي الكتاب قولان أحدهما أنه التوراة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r7.claim: The majority identify the Book they recite as the Torah.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r7.anchor: وفي الكتاب قولان أحدهما أنه التوراة قاله الجمهور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r8.claim: Another view identifies the Book as the Quran; on that reading, the addressees are not Jews.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p75/r8.anchor: والثاني أنه القرآن فلا يكون الخطاب على هذا القول لليهود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r1.claim: God rebukes the People of the Book for commanding the comprehensive good while failing to practice it themselves, despite reading Scripture and knowing the consequences; they should reason, awaken, and see clearly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى: كيف يليق بكم -يا معشر أهل الكتاب، وأنتم تأمرون الناس بالبر، وهو جماع الخير-

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r2.claim: Qatada says Israelites commanded obedience, piety, and good while acting otherwise, so God reproached them; al-Suddi agrees.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى: {أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم} قال: كان بنو إسرائيل يأمرون الناس بطاعة الله وبتقواه، وبالبر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the People of the Book and hypocrites urged fasting and prayer but failed to act on their own commands, for which God reproached them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: {أتأمرون الناس بالبر} أهل الكتاب والمنافقون كانوا يأمرون الناس بالصوم والصلاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r4.claim: Whoever commands something good should be among the quickest to do it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r4.anchor: فمن أمر بخير فليكن أشد الناس فيه مسارعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says they tell people not to disbelieve the prophethood and covenant in the Torah, while themselves rejecting God’s covenant to affirm His Messenger, breaking it, and denying what Scripture teaches.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وتنسون أنفسكم} أي: تتركون أنفسكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn Abbas that they urged people to enter Muhammad’s religion and observe prayer and other commands, while forgetting themselves.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك، عن ابن عباس في هذه الآية، يقول: أتأمرون الناس بالدخول في دين محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r7.claim: Abu al-Darda says full understanding requires detesting people for God’s sake, then turning to oneself and detesting oneself more.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r7.anchor: عن أبي قلابة في قول الله تعالى: {أتأمرون الناس بالبر وتنسون أنفسكم وأنتم تتلون الكتاب} قال: قال أبو الدرداء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r8.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r8.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says Jews would answer a question truthfully when no bribe or claim was involved, even as they neglected the same truth themselves; God rebuked them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p246#2/r8.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم في هذه الآية: هؤلاء اليهود إذا جاء الرجل يسألهم عن الشيء ليس فيه حق ولا رشوة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r1.claim: God rebukes them for neglecting their own practice of good; the fault is abandoning good, not instructing others while falling short themselves.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r1.anchor: والغرض أن الله تعالى ذمهم على هذا الصنيع ونبههم على خطئهم (4) في حق أنفسهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r2.claim: A learned person must command good and should practice it too, following Shuʿayb's refusal to act contrary to his instruction.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r2.anchor: كما قال شعيب، عليه السلام: {وما أريد أن أخالفكم إلى ما أنهاكم عنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r3.claim: The sounder position among early and later scholars is that both commanding right and practicing it are obligatory; neglecting one does not cancel the other.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r3.anchor: فكل من الأمر بالمعروف وفعله واجب، لا يسقط أحدهما بترك الآخر على أصح قولي العلماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r4.claim: Some say sinners must not forbid others' sins; Ibn Kathir calls this weak and says this verse gives them no proof.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r4.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى أن مرتكب المعاصي لا ينهى غيره عنها، وهذا ضعيف، وأضعف منه تمسكهم بهذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r5.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr told Rabiʿa that if only faultless people could enjoin good, no one would do so; Malik agreed that no one is without fault.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r5.anchor: قال مالك عن ربيعة: سمعت سعيد بن جبير يقول له: لو كان المرء لا يأمر بالمعروف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r6.claim: Knowing people are especially blameworthy when they knowingly leave obedience and commit sin; Ibn Kathir says this is why warnings about it occur in hadith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r6.anchor: فإنه ليس من يعلم كمن لا يعلم؛ ولهذا جاءت الأحاديث في الوعيد على ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r7.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r7.claim: Jundub reports the Prophet comparing a learned person who teaches good without practicing it to a lamp that lights others while burning itself; Ibn Kathir calls this route strange.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r7.anchor: عن جندب بن (1) عبد الله، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "مثل العالم الذي يعلم الناس الخير ولا يعمل به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r8.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r8.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's night-journey vision of people whose lips were cut with fiery shears, an image of those who instruct others in good but neglect themselves.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p247/r8.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "مررت ليلة أسري بي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p248/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p248/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p248/r1.claim: Anas's night-journey report about preachers' lips being cut is transmitted again by ʿAbd b. Humayd and several Ibn Mardawayh and Yazid b. Harun routes through Hammad; Ibn Mardawayh also gives a Thumama route mentioning tongues.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p248/r1.anchor: عن ثمامة، عن أنس، قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "مررت ليلة أسري بي على أناس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p248/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p248/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p248/r2.claim: Ibn Hibban, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmit through Malik b. Dinar, Thumama, and Anas a similar night-journey warning about preachers whose lips are cut.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p248/r2.anchor: عن مالك بن دينار، عن ثمامة، عن أنس بن مالك، قال: لما عرج برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مر بقوم تقرض شفاههم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p248/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p248/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p248/r3.claim: Usama reports the Prophet's warning that a man who preached good and forbade wrong without following his own advice will be dragged into Hell and confronted by those he instructed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p248/r3.anchor: عن أبي وائل، قال: قيل لأسامة -وأنا رديفه-: ألا تكلم عثمان؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r1.speaker: البخاري ومسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r1.claim: Bukhari and Muslim also transmit the Usama report about a preacher who commands good but does not practice it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r1.anchor: ورواه البخاري ومسلم، من حديث سليمان بن مهران الأعمش، به نحوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r2.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying God will pardon the unlettered on Judgment Day more readily than scholars; Ibn Kathir cites this to stress that knowledge increases responsibility.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r2.anchor: عن أنس، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله يعافي الأميين يوم القيامة ما لا يعافي العلماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r3.speaker: بعض الآثار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r3.claim: An unattributed report says the ignorant person is forgiven seventy times before the learned person is forgiven once, underscoring that the knowledgeable and unknowing are unequal.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r3.anchor: وقد ورد في بعض الآثار: أنه يغفر للجاهل سبعين مرة حتى يغفر للعالم مرة واحدة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir links the distinction between knowledgeable and unknowing people to the Qur'anic question whether those who know equal those who do not.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r4.anchor: وقال تعالى: {قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون إنما يتذكر أولو الألباب}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r5.speaker: الوليد بن عقبة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r5.claim: A report traced to the Prophet has people in Paradise ask people in Hell why they entered, since the saved learned from them; they answer that they preached but did not act. Ibn Asakir transmits it from al-Walid b. ʿUqba.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r5.anchor: وروى ابن عساكر في ترجمة الوليد بن عقبة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن أناسا من أهل الجنة يطلعون على أناس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas challenged a man who wanted to enjoin right to first examine three verses: this verse, the warning against saying what one does not do, and Shuʿayb's resolve to act consistently.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: إنه جاءه رجل، فقال: يا ابن عباس، إني أريد أن آمر بالمعروف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r7.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports a Prophetic warning that one who calls people to a deed or saying without doing it remains under God's anger until he stops or practices it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p249/r7.anchor: عن ابن عمر، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من دعا الناس إلى قول أو عمل ولم يعمل هو به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir says the chain of the Ibn ʿUmar report about calling people to what one does not practice is weak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r1.anchor: إسناده فيه ضعف، وقال إبراهيم النخعي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r2.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r2.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi disliked preaching stories because of this verse, the warning against saying what one does not do, and Shuʿayb's refusal to contradict his teaching.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r2.anchor: وقال إبراهيم النخعي: إني لأكره القصص لثلاث آيات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r3.speaker: مسلم بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r3.claim: Muslim b. ʿAmr's poem mocks a preacher who renounces worldly pleasures for others while seeking support and comfort for himself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r3.anchor:
وما أحسن ما قال مسلم بن عمرو:
ما أقبح التزهيد من واعظ … يزهد الناس ولا يزهد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r4.speaker: أبو عثمان الحيري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r4.claim: Abu ʿUthman al-Hiri likens an ungodly preacher urging piety to a physician who treats others while sick himself; the listeners wept.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: جلس أبو عثمان الحيري الزاهد يوما على مجلس التذكير فأطال السكوت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r5.speaker: أبو العتاهية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r5.claim: Abu al-ʿAtahiya says the preacher describes piety as though possessing it, while the scent of his sins exposes him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r5.anchor:
وقال أبو العتاهية الشاعر:
وصفت التقى حتى كأنك ذو تقى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r6.speaker: أبو الأسود الدؤلي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r6.claim: Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali says not to forbid a trait one practices; reform yourself first, then advice can be believed, followed, and useful.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r6.anchor:
وقال أبو الأسود الدؤلي:
لا تنه عن خلق وتأتي مثله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r7.speaker: عبد الواحد بن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r7.claim: Ibn Asakir recounts ʿAbd al-Wahid b. Zayd's dream-directed visit to Maimuna al-Sawda, whom he found praying among sheep and wolves that neither fled nor attacked.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r7.anchor: وذكر الحافظ ابن عساكر في ترجمة عبد الواحد بن زيد البصري العابد الواعظ قال: دعوت الله أن يريني رفيقي في الجنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r8.speaker: ميمونة السوداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r8.claim: Maimuna says her reconciliation with God brought reconciliation between wolves and sheep; she warns Ibn Zayd to inspect his limbs and says worldly gifts sought through repentance can replace intimacy with estrangement.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r8.anchor: يقال لها: ميمونة السوداء، فقصدت الكوفة لأراها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r9.speaker: ميمونة السوداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r9.claim: Maimuna's poem rebukes a preacher who scolds people for sins while himself remaining spiritually sick; if he had repented first, his words would find a truthful place in hearts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p250/r9.anchor: فقلت لها: عظيني. فقالت: يا عجبا من واعظ يوعظ، ثم قالت: يا ابن زيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251/r1.speaker: ميمونة السوداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251/r1.claim: Maimuna's continuing poem calls the preacher's own sinfulness a strange wrong and says his admonition would gain credibility if he first corrected or repented of his own misguidance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p251/r1.anchor: يا واعظا قام لا حساب … يزجر قوما عن الذنوب

JISHUMI:v1p359/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p359/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p359/r9.claim: Command is an utterance by a superior directing a subordinate to act; it is literal in speech and figurative in action because one controls words rather than deeds.
JISHUMI:v1p359/r9.anchor: الأمر: هو قول القائل لمن دونه: افعل، إذا أراد الآمر المأمور به، فهو حقيقة في القول مجاز في الفعل

JISHUMI:v1p359/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p359/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p359/r10.claim: Birr can mean kindness, purposeful benefit, obedience to God, or duty to relatives; the proverb about hirr and birr is variously explained as distinguishing kindness from hissing or a cat from a mouse.
JISHUMI:v1p359/r10.anchor: والبر: الإحسان، ورجل بر وبار، وفي المثل: لا يعرف الهر من البر

JISHUMI:v1p359/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p359/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p359/r11.claim: Birr derives from the breadth of good and is also the word for land as opposed to sea.
JISHUMI:v1p359/r11.anchor: وأصله من اتساع الخير، ومنه البر خلاف البحر

JISHUMI:v1p359/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p359/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p359/r12.claim: Nisyān, lapse, and heedlessness are related and oppose remembrance; forgetting is something leaving the self after being present, and it can mean abandoning, as in leaving God's remembrance and mercy.
JISHUMI:v1p359/r12.anchor: والنسيان والسهو والغفلة نظائر، ونقيضه الذكر، يقال: نسي نسيانا

JISHUMI:v1p359/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p359/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p359/r13.claim: One definition treats forgetting as the absence of necessary knowledge brought about by God.
JISHUMI:v1p359/r13.anchor: وهو عدم علم ضروري من فعل الله

JISHUMI:v1p359/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p359/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p359/r14.claim: Tilāwa means recitation; its root sense is following the letters.
JISHUMI:v1p359/r14.anchor: والتلاوة: القراءة، تلا يتلو: قرأ، وأصل التلاوة اتباع الحروف

JISHUMI:v1p359/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p359/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p359/r15.claim: Intellect, core, and knowledge are related; one account defines reason as a set of necessary cognitions that makes a person morally responsible.
JISHUMI:v1p359/r15.anchor: والعقل واللب والمعرفة نظائر، يقال: رجل عاقل، والعقل علوم ضرورية مجموعة إذا حصل في الإنسان صار مكلفا

JISHUMI:v1p359/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p359/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p359/r16.claim: Another account calls reason necessary knowledge of rational obligations and good or bad; it is likened to a hobble because it restrains wrongdoing.
JISHUMI:v1p359/r16.anchor: وآخر علوم العقل العلم بالواجبات العقلية والمحسنات والمقبحات، وسمي ذلك عقلا، تشبيها بالعقال

JISHUMI:v1p359/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p359/r17.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p359/r17.claim: Another definition describes reason as the capacity to infer the unseen from what is witnessed.
JISHUMI:v1p359/r17.anchor: وقيل: العقل قوة يمكن بها الاستدلال بالشاهد على الغائب

JISHUMI:v1p359/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p359/r18.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p359/r18.claim: Scholars differ on whether reason itself varies among people; one says it does not, another says it does although its judgments do not.
JISHUMI:v1p359/r18.anchor: واختلفوا فقيل: العقل لا يختلف، وقيل: يختلف وإن كان قضاياه لا تختلف

JISHUMI:v1p359/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p359/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p359/r19.claim: The scholars agree that this verse was revealed concerning the Jews.
JISHUMI:v1p359/r19.anchor: اتفقوا أن الآية نزلت في اليهود

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r1.claim: The interrogative hamza demands acknowledgment while rebuking them and expressing astonishment at their conduct.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r1.anchor: الهمزة للتقرير مع التوبيخ والتعجيب من حالهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r2.claim: Birr is expansive good and kindness, encompassing every good; its sense of breadth appears in the idiom “you spoke truth and acted kindly.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r2.anchor: والبر سعة الخير والمعروف ومنه البر لسعته ويتناول كل خير ومنه قولهم صدقت وبررت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r3.claim: Jewish scholars privately urged relatives and others they advised to follow Muhammad, yet did not follow him themselves.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r3.anchor: وكان الأحبار يأمرون من نصحوه في السر من أقاربهم وغيرهم باتباع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا يتبعونه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r4.claim: Another explanation is that they urged people to give alms but did not give themselves and misappropriated entrusted donations.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r4.anchor: وقيل كانوا يأمرون بالصدقة ولا يتصدقون واذا أتوا بصدقات ليفرقوها خانوا فيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r5.speaker: محمد بن واسع
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Wasiʿ relates that people in Hell will admit they told the people of Paradise to do deeds they themselves had contradicted.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r5.anchor: وعن محمد بن واسع بلغني ان ناسا من أهل الجنة اطلعوا على ناس من أهل النار فقالوا لهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r6.claim: They leave their own selves out of goodness as though they had forgotten them.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r7.claim: Reciting scripture intensifies the rebuke, as does the parallel phrase “while you know.”

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r8.claim: The Torah describes Muhammad or warns against betrayal, abandoning goodness, and failing to match deeds to words.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p161#4/r8.anchor: يعني تتلون التوراة وفيها نعت محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أو فيها الوعيد على الخيانة وترك البر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r1.claim: This grave rebuke asks why they do not recognize how ugly their conduct is and let reason’s rejection stop them; the passage echoes 21:67.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p162/r1.anchor: توبيخ عظيم بمعنى أفلا تفطنون لقبح ما أقدمتم عليه حتى يصدكم استقباحه عن ارتكابه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#2/r1.speaker: السدي، قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi and Qatada say they urged people to obey God while disobeying Him themselves; the cited line uses birr for obedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#2/r1.anchor: أحدها : أنهم كانوا يأمرون الناس بطاعة الله , وهم يعصونه , وهو قول السدي , وقتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says they urged people to hold to their Lord's Book but abandoned it by denying Muhammad's prophethood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#2/r2.anchor: والثاني : أنهم كانوا يأمرون الناس بالتمسك بكتاب ربهم ويتركونه بجحود ما فيه من نبوة محمد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#2/r3.claim: A third explanation is that they urged people to give charity while being stingy themselves.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p114#2/r3.anchor: والثالث : أنهم كانوا يأمرون بالصدقة ويضنون بها .

BURSEVI:v1p96/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p96/r2.claim: The rebuke addresses the Jews, and “the people” refers to their lower-status common folk.
BURSEVI:v1p96/r2.anchor: الخطاب لليهود والأمر القول لمن دونك افعل والمراد بالناس سفلتهم

BURSEVI:v1p96/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p96/r3.claim: Birr here means acknowledging the Prophet and following proofs; the word also conveys expansiveness, like the wide open plain.
BURSEVI:v1p96/r3.anchor: {بالبر} أي : الاعتراف بالنبي واتباع الأدلة وهو التوسع في الخير من البر الذي هو الفضاء الواسع

BURSEVI:v1p96/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p96/r4.claim: The interrogative hamza conveys confirmation together with rebuke and astonishment.
BURSEVI:v1p96/r4.anchor: الفضاء الواسع والهمزة تقرير مع توبيخ

BURSEVI:v1p96/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p96/r5.claim: Forgetting yourselves means leaving your own selves out of righteousness; the root sense of both forgetfulness and inattention is leaving, though inattention can concern the known or unknown and forgetting what was once present.
BURSEVI:v1p96/r5.anchor: {وتنسون أنفسكم} وتتركونها من البر كالمنسيات لأن أصل السهو والنسيان الترك إلا أن السهو يكون لما علمه الإنسان

BURSEVI:v1p96/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p96/r6.claim: The Jews secretly urged poor people with no benefit to them to believe Muhammad, but told wealthy people to wait because they saw only some signs of the end-time prophet, delaying their own adherence for advantage.
BURSEVI:v1p96/r6.anchor: كانوا يقولون لفقرائهم الذين لا مطمع لهم فيهم بالسر آمنوا بمحمد فإنه حق وكانوا يقولون للأغنياء نرى فيه بعض علامات نبي آخر الزمان

BURSEVI:v1p96/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p96/r7.claim: The same contradiction appears in a persistent sinner who vows to repent in old age but may be overtaken by death and left grieving the lost chance.
BURSEVI:v1p96/r7.anchor: وكذا حال من تمادى فى العصيان وهو يقول : أتوب عند الكبر والشيب وربما يفجأه الموت فيبقى في حسرة الفوت

BURSEVI:v1p96/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96/r8.speaker: حافظ
BURSEVI:v1p96/r8.claim: Hafez's image of the strutting partridge unaware of the falcon of fate illustrates how heedlessly people can overlook approaching death.
BURSEVI:v1p96/r8.anchor:
قال الحافظ :
ديدى آن قهقهة كبك خرامان حافظ

BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r1.claim: The book they recite is the Torah, which foretells the Prophet and commands belief in him.
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r1.anchor: والحال أنكم تتلون التوراة الناطقة بنعوته صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم الآمرة بالإيمان به

BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r2.claim: ʿAql originally means restraint, as in a camel hobble; it is named for restraining ugly conduct and holding a person to what is good.
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r2.anchor: والعقل في الأصل المنع والإمساك ومنه العقال الذي يشد به وظيف البعير

BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r3.claim: Intellect is a spiritual light by which the soul apprehends necessary and theoretical knowledge and is restrained from what is base.
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r3.anchor: سمي به النور الروحاني الذي به تدرك النفس العلوم الضرورية والنظرية لأنه يحبس عن تعاطي ما يقبح

BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r4.claim: Bursevī locates intellect in the brain because it is the seat of sensation.
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r4.anchor: ومحله الدماغ لأن الدماغ محل الحس

BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r5.speaker: عند البعض
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r5.claim: Some place intellect in the heart, which is the source of life and the sensory faculties.
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r5.anchor: وعند البعض محله القلب لأن القلب معدن الحياة ومادة الحواس

BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r6.speaker: عند البعض
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r6.claim: Another view identifies intellect as a light within the human body.
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r6.anchor: وعند البعض هو نور في بدن الآدمي

BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r7.claim: The rebuke targets neglecting one's own practice, not the act of commanding others to do good.
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r7.anchor: فمدار الإنكار والتوبيخ هي الجملة المعطوفة وهي جملة تنسون أنفسكم دون ما عطفت هي عليه

BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r8.claim: The verse does not forbid enjoining right when one falls short of practicing it: practice and exhortation are both duties, and neglecting one does not cancel the other.
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r8.anchor: ولا يستقيم قول من لا يجوز الأمر بالمعروف لمن لا يعمل به لهذه الآية بل يجب العمل به ويجب الأمر به

BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r9.speaker: عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r9.claim: The Prophet says to command what is right even without practicing it, and forbid wrong even while still committing it.
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r9.anchor: عليه السلام : "مروا بالمعروف وإن لم تعملوا به

BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r10.claim: Doing good while failing to do it remains good, but the exhorter should be quickest to practice what he urges and quickest to abandon what he forbids.
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r10.anchor: فالأمر بالحسن حسن وإن لم يعمل به ولكن قلما نفعت موعظة من لم يعظ نفسه

BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r11.claim: The verse urges the preacher to purify and perfect himself so that he can fulfill the truth and help others fulfill it; it does not bar a sinner from preaching.
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r11.anchor: والمراد بها حث الواعظ على تزكية النفس والإقبال عليها بالتكميل لتقوم بالحق وتقيم غيرها لا منع الفاسق من الوعظ

BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r12.claim: Bursevī begins an anecdote about an eloquent preacher whose sermons sometimes overwhelmed listeners, while an old woman kept her sensitive, righteous son from attending; the excerpt ends as she addresses the preacher.
BURSEVI:v1p96#2/r12.anchor: وكان كثيرا ما يموت من أهل مجلسه واحدا واثنان من شدة تأثير وعظه وكان في بلده عجوز لها ابن صالح رقيق القلب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r1.claim: The interrogative hamza calls the audience to account while expressing rebuke and astonishment at their conduct.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r1.anchor: للتقرير مع التوبيخ والتعجب من حالهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r2.claim: Birr is breadth of good and recognized virtue, from spaciousness, and includes every good; the idiom ‘you were truthful and dutiful’ exemplifies it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r2.anchor: أى سعة الخير والمعورف ومنه البر لسعته ويتناول كل خير

NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r3.speaker: الأحبار
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r3.claim: The rabbis privately told relatives and others to follow Muḥammad, but did not follow him themselves.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r3.anchor: من أقاربهم وغيرهم باتباع محمد عليه السلام ولا يتبعونه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r4.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r4.claim: Another explanation says they urged charity but did not give it themselves and misappropriated charity collected for distribution.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r5.claim: Forgetting themselves means leaving their own share of goodness as if they were forgotten.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r6.claim: This is a rebuke: they read the Torah, which describes Muḥammad, or warns against betrayal, abandoning goodness, and letting conduct contradict speech.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r6.anchor: وفيها نعت محمد عليه السلام أو فيها الوعيد على الخيانة وترك البر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r7.claim: The question rebukes them severely for failing to recognize their ugly conduct and let that recognition restrain them.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p41#3/r7.anchor: أفلا تفطنون لقبيح ما أقدمتم عليه حتى يصدكم استقباحه عن ارتكابه وهو توبيخ عظيم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r1.claim: The interrogative is a rebuke directed, in the commentators' account, at Jewish scholars.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r1.anchor: هذا استفهام معناه التوبيخ، والمراد في قول أهل التأويل علماء اليهود

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Jews in Medina told Muslim relatives and in-laws to remain in their faith, conceding that Muḥammad's command was true, while not following it themselves.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r2.anchor: كان يهود المدينة يقول الرجل منهم لصهره ولذي قرابته ولمن بينه وبينه رضاع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r3.claim: In another account from Ibn ʿAbbās, rabbis urged their followers to follow the Torah while themselves rejecting its description of Muḥammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r3.anchor: كان الأحبار يأمرون مقلديهم وأتباعهم باتباع التوراة، وكانوا يخالفونها في جحدهم صفة محمد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the rabbis encouraged obedience to God while committing sins themselves.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: كان الأحبار يحضون على طاعة الله وكانوا هم يواقعون المعاصي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r5.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r5.claim: Another group says they encouraged charity while being miserly; al-Qurṭubī says these explanations are close in meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r5.anchor: وقالت فرقة: كانوا يحضون على الصدقة ويبخلون. والمعنى متقارب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r6.speaker: بعض أهل الإشارات
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r6.claim: Some allusive interpreters understand the rebuke as demanding inward realities from others while contradicting one's own outward forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعض أهل الإشارات: المعنى أتطالبون الناس بحقائق المعاني وأنتم تخالفون عن ظواهر رسومها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r7.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r7.claim: Anas reports that on the Night Journey the Prophet saw worldly preachers' lips cut with fiery shears; Gabriel identified them as those who commanded righteousness but forgot themselves despite reciting scripture.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r7.anchor: عن أنس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r8.speaker: أبو أمامة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r8.claim: A report from Abū Umāma depicts people who preached good but forgot themselves dragging their intestines through Hell and identifying themselves as such preachers.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r8.anchor: وروى أبو أمامة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r9.claim: Al-Qurṭubī calls the Abū Umāma report weak because al-Ḥuṣayb ibn Jaḥdar was considered weak by Aḥmad and Ibn Maʿīn; Ibn Maʿīn considered Abū Ghālib sound in hadith.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r9.anchor: قلت: وهذا الحديث وإن كان فيه لين لأن في سنده الخصيب بن جحدر كان الإمام أحمد يستضعفه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r10.speaker: أسامة بن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r10.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says the meaning is transmitted in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim from Usāma ibn Zayd.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#2/r10.anchor: فقد رواه مسلم في صحيحه بمعناه عن أسامة بن زيد قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r1.speaker: أسامة بن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r1.claim: Muslim transmits from Usāma ibn Zayd a sound report of a man whose entrails spill into the Fire; he circles like a donkey at a mill and admits preaching what he did not practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r1.anchor: يؤتى بالرجل يوم القيامة فيلقى في النار فتندلق أقتاب بطنه فيدور بها كما يدور الحمار بالرحى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r2.claim: Qaṣab means intestine, its plural aqṣāb; aqṭāb is the plural of qitb, also an intestine; tandaliq means to emerge quickly, and another transmitted wording is تنفلق.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r2.anchor: القصب بضم القاف: المعى، وجمعه أقصاب. والأقتاب: الأمعاء، واحدها قتب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r3.claim: The sound report and verse show that a knowledgeable person who fails to do good or avoid wrong is punished more severely than an ignorant person, as one who disregards God's commands and gains no benefit from knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r3.anchor: فقد دل الحديث الصحيح وألفاظ الآية على أن عقوبة من كان عالما بالمعروف وبالمنكر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r4.claim: Al-Qurṭubī cites the report that the most severely punished on Judgment Day is a learned person whose knowledge did not benefit him, and attributes it to Ibn Mājah.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r4.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r5.claim: The rebuke concerns failing to practice righteousness, not the act of commanding righteousness itself.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r5.anchor: أن التوبيخ في الآية بسبب ترك فعل البر لا بسبب الأمر بالبر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r6.speaker: منصور الفقيه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r6.claim: Manṣūr al-Faqīh's poem calls those who command what they do not practice mad, unless they are literally struck by madness.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r6.anchor:
وقال منصور الفقيه فأحسن:
إن قوما يأمرونا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r7.speaker: أبو العتاهية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r7.claim: Abū al-ʿAtāhiya's poem rebukes one who describes piety while the stench of sins rises from his clothes.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r7.anchor:
وقال أبو العتاهية:
وصفت التقى حتى كأنك ذو تقى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r8.speaker: أبو الأسود الدؤلي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r8.claim: Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī says not to forbid a trait while practicing it; begin by correcting yourself so counsel is accepted and useful.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r8.anchor:
وقال أبو الأسود الدؤلي:
لا تنه عن خلق وتأتي مثله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو بن مطر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r9.claim: Abū ʿAmr ibn Maṭar recounts that Abū ʿUthmān al-Ḥīrī answered a request to speak with a poem comparing an ungodly preacher to a sick doctor treating patients.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#3/r9.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو بن مطر: حضرت مجلس أبي عثمان الحيري الزاهد فخرج وقعد على موضعه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان الحيري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r1.claim: After Abū ʿUthmān al-Ḥīrī's poem, the audience broke into weeping and commotion.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r2.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r2.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī disliked admonitory storytelling, citing this verse, 61:2, and Shuʿayb's words in 11:88.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r2.anchor: قال إبراهيم النخعي: إني لأكره القصص لثلاث آيات

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r3.speaker: سلم بن عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r3.claim: Salm ibn ʿAmr's poem mocks a preacher who renounces worldly life for listeners while seeking their support and not living by his advice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r3.anchor: وقال سلم بن عمرو: ما أقبح التزهيد من واعظ يزهد الناس ولا يزهد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r4.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r4.claim: When al-Ḥasan told Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh to counsel his companions and Muṭarrif feared saying what he did not do, al-Ḥasan replied that nobody does all he says; refusing to counsel would please Satan.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن لمطرف بن عبد الله: عظ أصحابك فقال إني أخاف أن أقول ما لا أفعل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says that if people could enjoin right and forbid wrong only when faultless, nobody would do so; Mālik agreed that everyone has some fault.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r5.anchor: سمعت سعيد بن جبير يقول: لو كان المرء لا يأمر بالمعروف ولا ينهى عن المنكر حتى لا يكون فيه شيء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r6.claim: Al-birr can mean obedience and good action, truthfulness, a fox's cub, or driving sheep; a cited idiom contrasts calling sheep with driving them, and poetry uses it for obedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r6.anchor: البر هنا الطاعة والعمل الصالح. والبر: الصدق. والبر: ولد الثعلب. والبر: سوق الغنم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r7.claim: In another poetic usage al-birr means the heart; with ḍamma it is familiar, while with fatḥa it denotes honoring and reverence, as in a dutiful child.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r7.anchor:
ويقال: إن البر الفؤاد في قوله:
أكون مكان البر منه ودونه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r8.claim: Here forgetting means leaving or neglecting; the same sense appears in 9:67, 6:44, and 2:237. The word can also mean the opposite of remembering or retaining.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#4/r8.anchor: والنسيان بكسر النون يكون بمعنى الترك وهو المراد هنا، وفي قوله تعالى: نسوا الله فنسيهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r1.claim: A hadith says Adam forgot, and his descendants consequently forget; al-Qurṭubī says the report will be discussed later.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r2.claim: Al-Qurṭubī gives نسيان as the verbal noun and cautions against vocalizing it as nisayān, associating that form with the dual of nisāʾ, a vein.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r2.anchor: وقد نسيت الشيء نسيانا، ولا تقل نسيانا بالتحريك لأن النسيان إنما هو تثنية نسا العرق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r3.claim: Anfus is a broken plural of nafs and is classified as a plural of paucity.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r4.claim: Nafs can mean spirit; al-Qurṭubī cites 39:42 and reports from Bilāl and the Prophet as evidence that the plural there means souls.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r4.anchor: ومن الدليل على أن النفس الروح قوله تعالى: الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r5.speaker: بلال
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r5.claim: In a report from Ibn Shihāb, Bilāl tells the Prophet that what took his soul had taken the Prophet's soul too.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r5.anchor: في قول بلال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث ابن شهاب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r6.claim: A report transmitted by Mālik from Zayd ibn Aslam has the Prophet say that God took their spirits and could have returned them at another time.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r6.anchor: وقوله عليه السلام في حديث زيد بن أسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r7.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r7.claim: Nafs can also mean blood, as in poetry about blood flowing on sword edges.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r7.anchor:
والنفس أيضا الدم يقال: سالت نفسه قال الشاعر:
تسيل على حد السيوف نفوسنا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r8.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r8.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī holds that an animal without flowing blood does not make water impure if it dies in it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r8.anchor: وقال إبراهيم النخعي: ما ليس له نفس سائلة فإنه لا ينجس الماء إذا مات فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r9.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r9.claim: Nafs may also mean the body; a poem describes the body or blood of al-Mundhir being brought into his house.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r9.anchor:
والنفس أيضا الجسد قال الشاعر:
نبئت أن بني سحيم أدخلوا أبياتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r10.claim: Reciting the Book makes the rebuke especially forceful; the Book is the Torah, and anyone acting in the same way shares their censure.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r10.anchor: السابعة: قوله تعالى: { وأنتم تتلون الكتاب } توبيخ عظيم لمن فهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r11.claim: Tilāwa means reading, originally derived from following words in sequence; the root also has other senses such as leaving, remainder, preserving, pursuing a due, and nearing death.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r11.anchor: وأصل التلاوة الاتباع، ولذلك استعمل في القراءة لأنه يتبع بعض الكلام ببعض في حروفه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r12.claim: The question asks why they do not restrain themselves from this ruinous behavior; ʿaql means restraint, as a camel's ʿiqāl prevents movement.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r12.anchor: الثامنة: قوله تعالى: { أفلا تعقلون } أي أفلا تمنعون أنفسكم من مواقعة هذه الحال المردية لكم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r13.claim: Blood compensation is called ʿaql because it restrains a victim's guardian from killing the offender; the word also describes restraint of the stomach and tongue and a fortified person.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r13.anchor: ومنه العقل للدية لأنه يمنع ولي المقتول عن قتل الجاني. ومنه اعتقال البطن واللسان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r14.claim: The word ʿaql can also mean a red textile used by Arab women to cover howdahs; the verse introducing ʿAlqama's poetic evidence appears here.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#5/r14.anchor: والعقل: ثوب أحمر تتخذه نساء العرب تغشى به الهوادج قال علقمة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r1.speaker: علقمة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r1.claim: ʿAlqama's verse calls a red textile عقل and contrasts it with رقم; المدموم means red here, though it can also mean a camel full of fat, and the terms name two kinds of cloth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r1.anchor: عقلا ورقما تكاد الطير تخطفه كأنه من دم الأجواف مدموم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r2.claim: Ibn Fāris says ʿaql is a textile pattern running lengthwise, whereas raqm is a round pattern.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r2.anchor: قال ابن فارس: والعقل من شيات الثياب ما كان نقشه طولا وما كان نقشه مستديرا فهو الرقم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r3.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says a rational person acts on what God obligates; someone who does not act accordingly is ignorant.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج: العاقل من عمل بما أوجب الله عليه، فمن لم يعمل فهو جاهل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r4.speaker: أهل الحق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r4.claim: The people of truth agree that reason exists and is created: if nonexistent it could not distinguish some beings, and if eternal it would rival God's eternity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r4.anchor: اتفق أهل الحق على أن العقل كائن موجود ليس بقديم ولا معدوم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r5.speaker: الفلاسفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r5.claim: Philosophers hold reason to be eternal; some call it a subtle substance in the body emitting a ray that distinguishes truths, while others call it a simple substance.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r5.anchor: وقد صارت الفلاسفة إلى أن العقل قديم ثم منهم من صار إلى جوهر لطيف في البدن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r6.speaker: طائفة من الفلاسفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r6.claim: One philosophical group locates reason in the brain as the seat of sensation; another locates it in the heart as the source of life and the senses.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r6.anchor: فقالت طائفة منهم: محله الدماغ لأن الدماغ محل الحس. وقالت طائفة أخرى: محله القلب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r7.claim: Al-Qurṭubī rejects reason as a substance: substances are alike, so if one substance were reason, every substance would have to be reason.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r7.anchor: وهذا القول في العقل بأنه جوهر فاسد، من حيث إن الجواهر متماثلة فلو كان جوهر عقلا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r8.claim: Defining reason as perceiving realities is closer than the substance theories but still wrong, since perception belongs to the living, whereas reason is an accident unable itself to perceive or desire.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r8.anchor: وقيل: إن العقل هو المدرك للأشياء على ما هي عليه من حقائق المعاني. وهذا القول وإن كان أقرب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r9.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري وأبو إسحاق الإسفرايني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r9.claim: Al-Ashʿarī, al-Isfarāyīnī, and other authorities define reason as knowledge, since one cannot reason without knowing or know without reasoning.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r9.anchor: وقال الشيخ أبو الحسن الأشعري والأستاذ أبو إسحاق الإسفرايني وغيرهما من المحققين: العقل هو العلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r10.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r10.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr defines reason as necessary knowledge of what is obligatory, possible, and impossible; Abū al-Maʿālī chose this in al-Irshād but in al-Burhān chose a capacity for acquiring knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r10.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر: العقل علوم ضرورية بوجوب الواجبات وجواز الجائزات واستحالة المستحيلات

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r11.speaker: المحاسبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r11.claim: Al-Muḥāsibī is reported to define reason as an innate disposition; the author notes that the judge's position is challenged and its error argued in al-Burhān.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r11.anchor: وحكي في البرهان عن المحاسبي أنه قال: العقل غريزة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r12.speaker: الشافعي وابن مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r12.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī and Ibn Mujāhid are reported to call reason an instrument of discrimination; al-Qalānisī calls it a discriminating faculty, and al-Muḥāsibī calls it lights and insights.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r12.anchor: وحكى الأستاذ أبو بكر عن الشافعي وأبي عبد الله بن مجاهد أنهما قالا: العقل آلة التمييز

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r13.speaker: الأستاذ أبو بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r13.claim: Al-Ustadh Abū Bakr doubts that al-Shāfiʿī and Ibn Mujāhid used the phrase instrument of discrimination; applying an instrument to an accident is metaphorical, and the other definitions are loose expressions.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r13.anchor: والأولى ألا يصح هذا النقل عن الشافعي ولا عن ابن مجاهد، فإن الآلة إنما تستعمل في الآلة المثبتة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r14.speaker: الأستاذ أبو بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r14.claim: Al-Ustadh Abū Bakr concludes that reason is neither a form nor a light but a means by which lights and insights are gained; al-Qurṭubī promises further discussion at the sūra's verse of divine unity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:44#6/r14.anchor: والعقل ليس بصورة ولا نور، ولكن تستفاد به الأنوار والبصائر. وسيأتي في هذه السورة بيان فائدته في آية التوحيد

RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r1.claim: The interrogative hamza in 'Do you command?' serves as a rhetorical rebuke and expresses astonishment at their conduct.
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r1.anchor: الهمزة في أتأمرون الناس بالبر للتقرير مع التقرير والتعجب من حالهم

RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r2.claim: Birr is a comprehensive name for good works; filial piety means obeying one's parents, and a righteous deed is one God approves.
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r2.anchor: البر فهو اسم جامع لأعمال الخير

RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r3.claim: Birr can also mean truthfulness, as in keeping an oath; 2:189 says righteousness belongs to the God-conscious, joining birr with taqwa.
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r3.anchor: وقد يكون بمعنى الصدق كما يقال بر في يمينه أي صدق ولم يحنث

RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r4.claim: Neglecting one's own good while urging others to do it is rationally repugnant: advice and compassion for others make no sense if one neglects oneself, so God rebukes them.
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r4.anchor: التغافل عن أعمال البر مع حث الناس عليها مستقبح في العقول

RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r5.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says they told people to obey God and avoid disobedience while abandoning obedience and committing sins themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r5.anchor: وهو قول السدي أنهم كانوا يأمرون الناس بطاعة الله وينهونه عن معصية الله

RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says they urged people to pray and give alms but failed to do so themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r6.anchor: قول ابن جريج أنهم كانوا يأمرون الناس بالصلاة والزكاة وهم كانوا يتركونهما

RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r7.claim: When privately asked about Muhammad, some said he was truthful and his cause right and urged people to follow him, yet did not follow him because they coveted gifts and payments from their followers.
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r7.anchor: إذا جاءهم أحد في الخفية لاستعلام أمر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم قالوا هو صادق فيما يقول وأمره حق فاتبعوه

RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r8.claim: Abū Muslim's preferred explanation is that Jews had foretold to Arab polytheists that a messenger would arise among them and urged them to follow him, but rejected him when he appeared.
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r8.anchor: فلما ظهر تركوه وأعرضوا عن دينه ، وهذا اختيار أبي مسلم

RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r9.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj says they commanded others to give charity while being miserly themselves, consistent with descriptions of their hardheartedness and consumption of usury and ill-gotten gain.
RAZI-FULL:v3p43/r9.anchor: وخامسها : هو قول الزجاج كانوا يأمرون الناس ببذل الصدقة وكانوا يشحون بها

RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r1.claim: One proposed context is Jewish hypocrites who publicly urged following Muhammad while inwardly rejecting him; God rebuked this inconsistency.
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r1.anchor: وسادسها : لهل المنافقين من اليهود كانوا يأمرون باتباع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في الظاهر ، ثم إنهم كانوا في قلوبهم منكرين له

RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r2.claim: Another proposed context is Jews urging others to follow the Torah, then rejecting its evidence for Muhammad's truth and refusing to believe in him.
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r2.anchor: وسابعها : أن اليهود كانوا يأمرون غيرهم باتباع التوراة ثم إنهم خالفوه لأنهم وجدوا فيها ما يدل على صدق محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r3.claim: Here forgetting cannot mean involuntary lapse after knowing, since an unintentional forgetful person is not accountable; it means neglecting one's own rights and interests.
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r3.anchor: فالنسيان عبارة عن السهو الحادث بعد حصول العلم والناسي غير مكلف ومن لا يكون مكلفا لا يجوز أن يذمه الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r4.claim: They read and study the Torah and know that it urges righteous acts and turning away from sinful acts.
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r4.anchor: فمعناه تقرأون التوراة وتدرسونها وتعلمون بما فيها من الحث على أفعال البر والإعراض عن أفعال الإثم

RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r5.claim: The question expresses astonishment at their conduct, as in 21:67.
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r5.anchor: تعجب للعقلاء من أفعالهم ونظيره قوله تعالى { أف لكم ولما تعبدون من دون الله أفلا تعقلون } [ الأنبياء : 67 ]

RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r6.claim: First, enjoining right and forbidding wrong rationally and scripturally aim to guide others, so preaching without self-reform is an irrational contradiction.
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r6.anchor: المقصود من الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر إرشاد الغير وذلك معلوم بشواهد العقل والنقل فمن وعظ ولم يتعظ فكأنه أتى بفعل متناقض

RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r7.claim: Second, a learned preacher who sins can embolden others: they may infer that he knows the warnings are baseless, making his conduct self-contradictory.
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r7.anchor: من وعظ الناس وأظهر علمه للخلق ثم لم يتعظ صار ذلك الوعظ سببا لرغبة الناس في المعصية

RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r8.claim: Third, a preacher seeks to make his admonition effective, while a sinner's conduct frustrates that aim; joining the two is irrational.
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r8.anchor: الثالث أن نت وعظ فلا بد وأن يجتهد في أن يصير وعظه مؤثرا في القلوب

RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r9.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r9.claim: Ali said that two men broke his back: an openly transgressive scholar and an ignorant person devoted to worship.
RAZI-FULL:v3p44/r9.anchor: ولهذا قال علي رضي الله عنه : قصم ظهري رجلان عالم متهتك وجاهل متنسك

RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r1.claim: Some argue that a sinner may not enjoin right or forbid wrong, citing this rebuke and 61:2–3, and the absurdity of an adulterer correcting a partner's uncovered face during adultery.
RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : ليس للعاصي أن يأمر بالمعروف وينهى عن المنكر واحتجوا بالآية والمعقول

RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r2.claim: The accountable person has two duties, avoiding sin and restraining others; failure in one does not cancel the other. The verse forbids neglecting oneself generally, not enjoining good while imperfect.
RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r2.anchor: المكلف مأمور بشيئين : أحدهما ترك المعصية ، والثاني منع الغير عن فعل المعصية والإخلال بأحد التكليفين لا يقتضي الإخلال بالآخر

RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r3.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that blame in the verse proves human acts are not created by God: compulsion would make reproach as senseless as asking a black person to become white.
RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r3.anchor: احتجت المعتزلة بهذه الآية على أن فعل العبد غير مخلوق لله عز وجل فقالوا قوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi argues that an undetermined choice would be chance and unblameworthy; a human determiner restarts the inquiry, while a divine determiner makes the opposite impossible, so their objection rebounds on them.
RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r4.anchor: وإن حصل من الله تعالى فعند حصوله يصير ذلك الطرف راجحا والآخر مرجوحا والمرجوح ممتنع الوقوع

RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r5.claim: His ultimate answer is that God is not questioned about what He does.
RAZI-FULL:v3p44#2/r5.anchor: ثم الجواب الحقيقي عن الكل : أنه ' لا يسأل عما يفعل '

RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r1.claim: Anas reports that on the Night Journey the Prophet saw people whose lips were cut with fiery shears; Gabriel identified them as worldly preachers who urged good but neglected themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r1.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال عليه الصلاة والسلام مررت ليلة أسري بي على قوم تقرض شفاههم بمقاريض من النار

RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r2.claim: The Prophet described a man in Hell whose stench torments its people, identifying him as a scholar who did not benefit from his knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r2.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام إن في النار رجلا يتأذى أهل النار بريحه فقيل من هو يا رسول الله

RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r3.claim: The Prophet likened one who teaches people goodness without practicing it to a lamp that lights others while burning itself.
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r3.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام مثل الذي يعلم الناس الخير ولا يعمل به كالسراج يضيء للناس ويحرق نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r4.speaker: الشعبي
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿbi relates that people in Paradise ask people in Hell why they entered after the former gained Paradise through their teaching; they reply that they preached good without doing it.
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r4.anchor: وعن الشعبي : يطلع قوم من أهل الجنة إلى قوم من النار فيقولون لم دخلتم النار ونحن إنما دخلنا الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r5.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r5.claim: A saying contrasts ineffective verbal counsel with counsel by deed, whose arrows reach their target.
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r5.anchor: كما قيل : من وعظ بقوله ضاع كلامه ، ومن وعظ بفعله نفذت سهامه

RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r6.speaker: الشاعر
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r6.claim: The poem urges a teacher to reform himself first; once he avoids vice, others accept his advice, follow his example, and benefit from his teaching.
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r6.anchor: وقال الشاعر : يا أيها المعلم غيره … هلا لنفسك كان ذا التعليم

RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r7.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r7.claim: A saying holds that one person's deeds among a thousand speak more effectively than a thousand people's words directed to one.
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r7.anchor: قيل : عمل رجل في ألف رجل أبلغ من قول ألف رجل في رجل

RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r8.claim: One who both counsels others and acts on the counsel has a great station with God.
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r8.anchor: وأما من وعظ واتعظ فمحله عند الله عظيم

RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r9.speaker: يزيد بن هارون
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r9.claim: In a dream after his death, preacher and ascetic Yazid ibn Harun said God forgave him; he answered Munkar and Nakir that after decades calling people to God, they should not ask who his Lord was.
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r9.anchor: روي أن يزيد بن هارون مات وكان واعظا زاهدا فرؤي في المنام فقيل له ما فعل الله بك

RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r10.speaker: الشبلي
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r10.claim: At al-Shibli's death, when asked to say there is no god but God, he replied that a house inhabited by God needs no lamps.
RAZI-FULL:v3p45/r10.anchor: وقيل للشبلي عند النزع قل لا إله إلا الله فقال
